Hi Magda, 

From GDPR perspective, the disclosure of personal data should be strictly limited to what is mandatory for the document to constitute a valid invoice.

Under PL VAT Act, the invoice should directly identify both parties of the transaction, so if the courier would deal directly with the end-user, the disclosure of their name would be permissible under GDPR. However where the party to the transaction is the fleet and not the courier directly, the name of the courier is outside the scope set out in the VAT Act and therefore should not be included in the invoice.

BR,

Adriana

Thank you for the feedback. Before I will do more research on that, I wanted to check with you if we covered this already. Right now I see 3 major topics:

* *Monitoring* (the privacy notice for employees includes *Performance related information* (such as objectives, work results, time tracking and attendance information, career plans). Monitoring work performance is ok but it should not be disproportionate and excessive. Here we would collect how much is monitored and what happens to this data (even if this may include labor law aspects, the collection is limited to data protection). If the extent of the current  monitoring is justifiable, we should at least tell the responsible authorities when things will become critical (checking toilet breaks,…).

* *Data Retention:* Based on the purpose of the data collection there should be a tight retention period (Specially if the data is used to optimise ware houses, anonymised data would be possible swell)

* *Transparency:* The term *Performance related information* does not seem very transparent.

* *DSAR:* We raise this because of the experience with working unions (other verticals). Based on the news coverage (Amazon warehouses in Europe) this could be an issue.

Right now I am not aware of any complaints. I will check with Matheus and after that we will reach out to them (based on a prioritisation). Before that, I would of course inform you and SIlja in advance.

Hi Anna, there is no need to do anything else from OPS side. The orders of this provider looked suspicious with high velocity of requests per user. 

We have 2 blacklists that we can add providers to, in order to prevent fraudulent users from requesting from said providers.

* *3DS Blacklist* - this is a fraud rule that contains a list of providers whose clients will be subjected to a 3DS authorization check *if* they meet certain criteria set by fraud. The advantage of this is that it’s a solution that creates the least amount of friction for the provider. If they are a legitimate provider, they might not even notice a change. If the eater is legitimate, they will pass authorization and be able to order just as usual. In this case, providers that are targeted by fraudsters are actually protected.
* *Reject blacklist.* The scenario is very similar. For providers in this blacklist, eaters that meet our criteria will not be able to order at all.

Simply put, if the users are fraudulent, they will have to pass authorization but will still be able to order from this provider if they do. Users that do not meet our criteria will not experience any friction at all.

Please don’t hesitate to respond here if you have any other questions :)

COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN CAST(u.created as date) >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -365, current_date) as date) THEN u.id END ) AS year_accounts_created, 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN uc.COMMENT LIKE ('%robbery%') THEN u.id END) AS blocked_for_robbery
FROM
glue.ng_pii.user_user AS u
LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.user_user_comment AS uc ON uc.user_id = u.id
WHERE
u.email IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING
(COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN CAST(u.created as date) >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date) THEN u.id END ) > 3 AND COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN CAST(u.created as date) >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) as date) THEN u.id END ) > 8)
OR (COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN uc.COMMENT LIKE ('%robbery%') THEN u.id END) > 1 AND COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN CAST(u.created as date) >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) as date) THEN u.id END ) > 3)
OR (COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN uc.COMMENT LIKE ('%robbery%') THEN u.id END) > 3 AND COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN CAST(u.created as date) >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -365, current_date) as date) THEN u.id END ) > 3)
ORDER BY 3 DESC{code}

Hey [~accountid:5aab754b5c335d2a73a795f4] \!

*In short* - Driver’s insurance company details can be provided to the rider under legitimate interest legal basis. 

Drivers provide the transportation service to the passenger and are therefore also liable to any claims arising in connection to the provision of transportation services. 

If an accident occurs during the trip where passenger suffers direct and/or indirect damage, then they may need to pursue a claim against the transport service provider (driver).  In order to assure access to justice (opportunity to submit a claim), the passenger needs to know the insurance company details. 

As Bolt would only provide insurance company details, then it would be purposeful and limited. 

Driver Privacy Notice will be updated to cover that Bolt may disclose driver insurance details to passengers. 

*Things to keep in mind:*

* Details should be provided based on individual rider request;
* There needs to be enough information in the request to identify the trip and the driver in question. 
* Description of incident should be provided by the rider (that it is clear that passenger is asking for the details in order to pursue a claim subsequent to an accident/incident).

Hi [~accountid:6242def45f63fd0069b130bd] and [~accountid:624407b42e101c006a8d8cf6] 

please find below external counsel’s feedback on your query both from the angle of financial law - given the electronic money flow- and consumer law.  

The analysis is quite complex, let me know if you want to discuss it over a call.

Otherwise, please let me know if  in the light of the below you want to move forward and you need further assistance. 

 ***

“We revert back to you regarding the questions raised on the vouchers that you consider to issue. We will first analysis the potential qualification as electronic-money (“*e-money*”) in the sense of article L. 315-1 of the French monetary and financial Code (“*FMFC*”) and second the civil and consumer law aspects.

 

Indeed, Bolt would like to buy second hand cars from private individuals in order to integrate these ones in its fleet of vehicles. The seller could receive, instead of an amount in euros, a voucher of an equivalent amount, usable to access to the Bolt services. The amount of credits could be used in order to pay the rides made with the Bolt app. The credits shall not be used to access to others services, from Bolt or from others services providers.

 

*I.*                +*On the e-money questions and potential exemption*+

 

# +*On the nature of e-money of the credits/vouchers*+

 

The notion of electronic money in French law is based on the transposition of the second e-money directive. In this respect, Article L. 315-1, I of the FMFC states that:

_« electronic money is a monetary value that is stored in electronic, including magnetic, form, representing a claim on the issuer, that is issued against the remittance of funds for the purpose of payment transactions as defined in Article L. 133-3 and that is accepted by a natural or legal person other than the electronic money issuer”_

 

Therefore, electronic money can be analysed as :

(i) a value having a monetary function; and

(ii) stored in electronic format; and

(iii) representing a receivable against its issuer; and

(iv) issued against the delivery of funds for the purpose of making payment transactions.

 

In other words, under French and European law, electronic money is:

* a substitute for euro coins and banknotes only (the euro being the only currency legally recognised in France under the Article L. 111-1 of *FMFC*);
* issued for the execution of payment transactions of limited amount;
* prepaid; and

* redeemable, at the first request of the holder, by the remittance of euro coins or banknotes or by a transfer of euro funds.

 

In the present case, it seems that the voucher issued by Bolt :

* has a monetary function, since it allow to pay for rides made with the Bolt app and represent an equivalent amount of the value of the cars sold to Bolt by the individuals. As mentioned the seller will have credits (representing an amount equivalent to euros) allowing to pay for some transactions. In the example given the amount of credits will be equivalent to the amount of euros of the value of the car sold;
* we understand that the vouchers / credits will be stored electronically: the voucher holder will be able to consult and use its credits electronically. The amount of the vouchers will be splitable in different unit to pay the price of each ride made with the app;
* the seller will have a claim on the issuer on the issuer / Bolt: Bolt will guarantee the amount of credits due to the credits’ holder;
* the prepaid nature will be ensure by the “charging” when the car’s owner sell its car to Bolt. Bolt will charge an amount of credits equivalent to the value of the car in euros.

 

*Conclusion:* +*we do believe that the vouchers/credits issued as a counterparty of the car sold to Bolt, representing an amount equivalent of the price of the vehicle, representing a monetary value, can be considered as fulfilling the characteristics of e-money.*+

 

Please note that the FMFC implements some charging thresholds to respect. In particular +*the monetary value electronically stored and usable thanks to physical support is limited to €10.000*+ (in accordance with Article D. 315-2 of the FMFC).

 

# +*On the benefit by Bolt of exemption*+

 

By principle the e-money institutions are the only entities, with the credit institutions (commonly called “banks”), allowed to issue and reimburse e-money.



Nonetheless, the FMFC provides for some exemptions, including in particular ” (in accordance with Article L. 525-5 of the FMFC).

* when the e-money is issued and managed by a company only for the purchase of a determined good or service *from the company (issuer) itself* or from company linked in a commercial franchise. In that model, the e-money is only accepted by the issuer, there is no external acceptors. In practice that exemption corresponds very often to the gift cards usable in the shop of the issuer. In the present situation, we do believe that we can consider that the voucher is charged not by the remittance of legal tenders but by compensation with the price of the vehicle (Subject to the specific analysis on that point). The voucher/credits will be usable *only*  on the Bolt’s app in order to pay rides. The credit cannot be used outside the platform. No third parties, any circumstances will accept the voucher/credit as a payment means. We therefore believe that we have strong elements in order to argue that there is no acceptors and that Bolt can benefit from the exemption.
* when the e-money is accepted in a “limited network” or to access to “a limited range of goods and services.” Under that exemption the e-money should only enable to access to a very range of goods and services, or should be accepted in a very limited network. We do believe that the criteria can be met since (1) the vouchers only enable to access to Bolt’s rides and (2) the vouchers can only be used on the Bolt app, to the exclusion to any other acceptors. The competent Authority (“_Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de resolution””_*ACPR”)* must be informed if the volume of payment exceed *1 million euros per year.*  In practice, and in the light of the last publications of the Authority, the volume of the payment will be strong point of attention of the regulator.

 

Please note that the ACPR has issued a guidance on the LNE ([version revised on July 2022)|https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/acpr.banque-france.fr/sites/default/files/media/2022/08/09/20220720_position_2022-p-01.pdf__;!!NknhfzgzgQ!1_eiwrQWJbqsATx5HImpUbyEHhvZTD_eY49H9RNlRx_Z2S6kKGp5cazDLh8Vi6VCijlIE1K5TU29WE0Bj9ACZeKQIhk2zC3d__9N$] and recalls that with respect to the exemptions granted to date by the ACPR's Supervisory Board, the criterion of a limited range of goods or services has been assessed, in particular, from the perspective of whether the goods or services belong to a "theme" that is sufficiently specific not to be confused with a "universal", i.e., general, payment method. Thus, the ACPR's Supervisory Board has refused to exempt payment methods used for the acquisition of goods or services belonging to a thematic offer that is too broad, such as the themes "wedding lists" or "birth", which cover an extremely wide range of goods or services, or belonging to several thematic offers (for example, online games and music). In the present case the credits can only be used to access to Bolt’s rides and seems by nature restricted.

 

In addition to examining the functional link, the ACPR takes the following criteria into account in its assessment, depending on the size and specificity of the market concerned :

_”-_ +_the volume and value of payment transactions to be carried out using the payment instruments_+ _on an annual the volume and value of the payment transactions to be carried out using the payment instruments on an annual basis, as envisaged by the company_

* the maximum amount to be credited to the payment instruments, as contemplated by the business

* the maximum number of payment instruments to be issued, as contemplated by the business; and

* the risks to which the user is exposed by using the payment instrument, as identified by the identified by the business.

_Note: A single exempt payment instrument may not be used for more than one limited range of goods and of goods and services.  the volume of goods and services that can be acquired under the exemption can be taken into account, without a maximum threshold having been defined._ ” (we underlined)

 

In the same way, regarding the limited network of acceptor the ACPR will take into consideration the volume and the nature of the limited network of acceptors:

_”_ _Depending on the size and specificity of the market concerned, other objective criteria that are also taken into account by the ACPR are taken into account by the ACPR are_

* the limited geographical scope: the network of acceptors of the means of payment must be limited geographically and not intended to expand (shopping centre, shops in a town centre, local stores in a city centre, local authority, etc.). An exemption was granted by the ACPR for a market place marketing the products of merchants located in the same local community local authority;

* 

+_the maximum number of goods and services providers operating within the network limited_+_, as indicated by the company in the exemption declaration;_

* the volume and value of payment transactions to be carried out with the payment instruments on an annual basis, as instruments on an annual basis, as envisaged by the undertaking;

* 

+_the maximum amount to be credited to the payment instruments_+_, as envisaged by the undertaking_

* the maximum number of payment instruments to be issued, as envisaged by the undertaking; and

* the risks to which the user is exposed by using the exempt payment instrument, as instrument, as identified by the firm.” 

” (we underlined)

 

 

*Conclusion*: +*Therefore, it seems possible, in theory,  to consider that Bolt may benefit from an exemption to the obligation to be register as an e-money institution or a distributor of an e-electronic institution (if a partnership can be considered) either due to the fact the vouchers is only accepted by the issuer itself or due to the fact that the vouchers only enable to access to a limited range of services(namely the Bolt’s rides).*+

 

A *more detailed analysis* should be performed in the light of:

# the foreseen flow-charts;
# the anticipated volume of activities; and
# the exact functionnalities and restrictions regarding the possible use of the vouchers.

 

*The ACPR will be cautious on the anticipated volume of transactions/ amounts charged in vouchers.*  As mentioned above, the ACPR recently reinforced its doctrine and is performing a more in-depth analysis in order to assess if an entity may benefit from an exemption. In the present case, the amounts that can be considered (subject to a more precise analysis but the amounts are potentially in thousands of euros) and the total volume of transactions can be high (subject to the 1M disclosure threshold mentioned). In addition, the ACPR may raise some concerned on (1) the geographical limitation of the use of the voucher and (2) the safeguarding measures protecting the funds of the customers.

 

*II.*                  +*Civil and consumer law issues*+

 

In our opinion, the purchase by Bolt of cars belonging to consumers can follow two different schemes:

 

* +*First scheme*+*:* Sale contract (1) + Transfer in lieu of payment (2)

 

# *A sale contract*: Under French law, a sale is an agreement by which one party undertakes to deliver a good and the other to pay for it. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the contract is considered as fully executed, and ownership is acquired to the buyer, as soon as the good and the price are agreed, even though the good has not yet been delivered or the price paid.

 

* Taking your below example, the sale contract is considered as executed once Bolt and the consumer have agreed on the vehicle to be sold and the price to be paid.

 

# *Transfer in lieu of payment*: The creditor may agree to receive in payment something other than what is due to him. The agreement between the creditor and the debtor relating to this method of performance and extinction of the obligation must take place +after+ the contract has been concluded.

 

* *Here, the consumer could therefore agree to receive the price of the car sold in the form of Bolt Credits to be used on Bolt Drive. However, this consent should normally occur only after the sale contract has been concluded. As such,* +*Bolt would need to request the express consent from the consumer to receive payment in the form of a voucher on Bolt Drive, after the sale contract has been concluded. The consumer would therefore always be in a position to refuse it and thus require payment of the sum.*+

 

* +*Second scheme*+*:* Sale contract (1) + Contract for the deposit of money (2) + Debt set-off (3).

# *A sale contract* (see above).

 

# *A contract for the deposit of money*: The French Civil Code defines the deposit as an act by which one party receives (the depositary) something from another (the depositor), with the obligation to keep it and return it in kind. The agreement of both parties is required. The depositary must not use the thing deposited without the depositor’s permission and must return the same amount as he receives. The deposit must be returned to the depositor as soon as he claims it, +even if the contract has fixed a specific time limit+ for its return.

 

* In the case of the purchase of a consumer’s car by Bolt, it would be necessary to provide in the terms that the consumer agrees that the amount to be paid for the sale will be deposited to Bolt and that this amount can be used at any time to use the Bolt Drive service (see point 3).

 

* It would also be necessary to inform the consumer that he can ask for the return of the deposited sum *at any time*. Should this information not be provided to consumers before they agree to the sale of their car, the practice could be deemed unfair or even misleading as it would omit a substantial information (here, the fact that the consumer can ask for the payment in money at any time, and that he/she is thus not bound to use the Bolt Credits until exhaustion).

 

* It is therefore our analysis that preventing the consumer from obtaining payment in money for the sale of their car would very likely be deemed unfair to consumer, as they may be forced to use the service when they do not want to (at all or no longer) and, if they no longer wish to use it, they will loose the price of their car and so will never have received full payment.

 

# *A debt set*-*off*: The set-off is the simultaneous extinction of reciprocal obligations between two persons. Set-off shall only take place between two +fungible+, +certain+, +liquid+ and +due+ obligations:

* Fungible means something that can be replaced by a similar one. This is the case of money;
* Certain means that the debt must not be conditional, _i.e._ it must not be subordinated to the uncertain occurrence of a future event;
* Liquid means that the debt must be certain in their existence and their amount must be known;
* Due means that the creditor is entitled to claim payment (which is not the case, for example, when the term deadline to pay has not yet expired).

 

* In practice, this means that the Bolt debt for the payment of the price of the car could only be set-off progressively, as the consumer uses the service. Before such use of the service, Bolt’s receivable against the consumer is neither certain, nor liquid, nor due. If the consumer stop using the service at one point, he could still claim for the payment of the remaining of his debt as no off-setting would be possible, in the absence of a Bolt’s receivable against the consumer.

 

* *In our opinion, it would therefore not be possible to prevent the consumer from claiming the payment in money of the car’s price if the consumer does not use the service, as Bolt would not have any receivable against the consumer.*

 

Finally, please note that purchasing second-hand cars would also raise some regulatory issues, such as:

* Specific administrative formalities pertaining to the change of owner of the car;
* Risks regarding concealment of stolen goods and money laundering.”

{code:sql}SELECT
        k.key,
        COUNT(DISTINCT k.user_id) AS count_of_users,
        COUNT(DISTINCT k.orders_id) AS count_of_cash_campaign_orders,
        SUM(k.price) AS amount_of_cash_paid,
        SUM(k.predicted) AS amount_of_predicted_price,
        SUM(k.predicted) - SUM(k.price) as campaign_amount,
        (SUM(k.predicted) - SUM(k.price) * 1.0)/ SUM(k.predicted) AS percent_campaign_covered
    FROM
        (
        SELECT 
        etl.order_id AS orders_id,
        CAST(fu.email AS varchar) || ':' || CAST(o.campaign_code AS varchar) || ':' || CAST(etl.country_code AS varchar) as key, 
            etl.order_id as id, etl.user_id as user_id, 
            etl.user_price_eur as price, 
            cpd.predicted_price / etl.eur_currency_rate as predicted
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
LEFT JOIN ng_public.company_order AS o ON etl.order_id = o.id AND etl.city_id = o.city_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public.company_order_try ot ON etl.order_id = ot.order_id AND etl.city_id = ot.city_id AND ot.order_id = o.id
LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.pricing_order_prediction as cpd ON etl.city_id = cpd.city_id and cpd.order_id = etl.order_id 
LEFT JOIN glue.ng_pii.user_user as fu ON etl.user_id = fu.id 
WHERE
etl.order_type = 'rides'
AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
AND ot.state = 'finished'
AND etl.payment_method_group = 'cash'
AND o.campaign_code is not NULL
AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND o.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND o.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND ot.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND ot.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND cpd.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5,6 
) AS k 
GROUP BY
        1
HAVING
        COUNT(DISTINCT k.user_id) > 3
        and (SUM(k.predicted) - SUM(k.price)) > 0{code}

*order_fraud_driver_self_campaign*

{code:sql}SELECT CAST(etl.city_id AS varchar) || ':' || CAST(etl.order_id AS varchar) as key,
                1 as fraud_campaign_self_order
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
JOIN ng_public.company_order AS co ON etl.order_id = co.id AND etl.city_id = co.city_id
JOIN ng_public.company_order_try ot ON etl.order_id = ot.order_id AND etl.city_id = ot.city_id AND ot.order_id = co.id
JOIN glue.ng_public.fraud_order_check as oc ON oc.order_id = etl.order_id AND oc.city_id = etl.city_id 
JOIN glue.ng_public.fraud_order_check_result as ocr ON ocr.order_check_id = oc.id
            WHERE  etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.state='finished'
                AND co.campaign_code IS NOT NULL
                AND ot.price<>ot.ride_price
                AND ot.price_review_status='ok'
                AND ocr.type IN ('SAME_RIDER_DRIVER_DEVICE', 'SAME_RIDER_DRIVER_EMAIL', 'SAME_RIDER_DRIVER_NAME', 'SAME_RIDER_DRIVER_PHONE')
            GROUP BY 1{code}

{code:sql}SELECT CAST(etl.city_id AS varchar) || ':' || CAST(etl.order_id AS varchar) as key,
                1 as fraud_campaign_repetitive_order
           FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
JOIN ng_public.company_order AS co ON etl.order_id = co.id AND etl.city_id = co.city_id
JOIN ng_public.company_order_try ot ON etl.order_id = ot.order_id AND etl.city_id = ot.city_id AND ot.order_id = co.id
JOIN glue.ng_public.fraud_order_check as oc ON oc.order_id = etl.order_id AND oc.city_id = etl.city_id 
JOIN glue.ng_public.fraud_order_check_result as ocr ON ocr.order_check_id = oc.id
 LEFT JOIN ng_public.currency_exchange_rates r ON DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(etl.created) AND r.currency = ot.price_currency
            WHERE  etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.state='finished'
                AND co.campaign_code IS NOT NULL
                AND ot.price<>ot.ride_price
                AND ot.price_review_status='ok'
                AND (ocr.type='REPETITIVE_RIDER_RIDE'  OR ocr.type LIKE 'REPETITIVE_ORDER_BY_%')
                AND etl.city_id NOT IN (993,997,991,1167)
            GROUP BY 1,ot.ride_price, r.rate, ot.price
            HAVING (
            ((ot.ride_price/NULLIF(r.rate,0)-ot.price/NULLIF(r.rate,0))/NULLIF(ot.ride_price/NULLIF(r.rate,0),0)) BETWEEN 0.25 AND 0.4 
            AND (ot.ride_price/NULLIF(r.rate,0)-ot.price/NULLIF(r.rate,0))>=1
            )
                OR (ot.ride_price/NULLIF(r.rate,0)-ot.price/NULLIF(r.rate,0))/NULLIF(ot.ride_price/NULLIF(r.rate,0),0) >=0.4{code}

Just a sample use case that we recently encountered in the Delivery → Provider domain. We had to create a new service for exposing price history of delivery menu items. We did that and used TiDB for the storage layer, but then we had to backfill prices for the last 6 months.

In order to do so, he had 2 alternatives:

* A) Move data from MySQL to TiDB and execute some queries to transform data (obviously, with the help of DBAs)
* B) Obtain live database access and execute a script locally to move data from one DB to the other (while also transforming it using Typescript)

The second approach has the benefit of implementing the transformation logic in Typescript (which makes the whole process a lot easier), but it lacks transparency and the ability to audit the script’s execution.

* Created test instance and tested feature. It needs these settings in my.cnf and{color:#ff5630} *server restart* {color}

{noformat}extra_port=33062
extra_max_connections=10{noformat}
* To connect using reserved extra port:

{noformat}mysql --defaults-file=/etc/mysql/debian.cnf --port=33062 --protocol=tcp{noformat}
* Playbook to add options to my.cnf

{noformat}leandro@sqldb-ansible:~/github/db-mysql-ansible$ cat add_extra_port.yaml
---
- hosts: all  #tag_role_db
  become: yes

  tasks:
  - name: Check mysql version
    mysql_variables:
      variable: version
      config_file: "/etc/mysql/debian.cnf"
    register: myver
  - debug:
      var: myver

  - name: avoid duplicate extra_port
    ini_file:
      path: /etc/mysql/my.cnf
      section: mysqld
      option: extra_port
      state: absent
      create: no
    when: myver.msg is search("5.7.28")

  - name: avoid duplicate extra_max_connections
    ini_file:
      path: /etc/mysql/my.cnf
      section: mysqld
      option: extra_max_connections
      state: absent
      create: no
    when: myver.msg is search("5.7.28")

  - name: add extra_port and extra_max_connections
    lineinfile:
      path: /etc/mysql/my.cnf
      line: "extra_port=33062\nextra_max_connections=10"
      insertafter: '^max_connections.*'
    when: myver.msg is search("5.7.28")

#eu-north-1
time ansible-playbook -i north_aws_ec2.yaml add_extra_port.yaml --limit '*-d7'

        (COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) * 1.00)/ COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) AS fraud_payment_ratio
            FROM (
            WITH inputs AS (
SELECT 
d.id AS calculation_id,
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.device_additional_info.device_fingerprint') AS device_fingerprint
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request AS d
WHERE 
d.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
                SELECT etl.order_id AS order_id,
                i.device_fingerprint AS device_fingerprint, etl.country_code AS country_code, etl.user_id AS user_id, 
                CASE WHEN etl.is_chargeback OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payments,
                CASE WHEN etl.is_final_failed_payment THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END AS failed_payments
                FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
                LEFT JOIN inputs AS i ON i.calculation_id = etl.fraud_calculation_id AND i.user_id = etl.user_id
                WHERE  etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
                GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6
                ) AS k
                GROUP BY
                1
            HAVING
                COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id)
                 > 1
               AND COUNT(DISTINCT k.user_id)
                 > 2
               AND COUNT(DISTINCT k.user_id)
                 < 5000
               AND ( (COUNT(DISTINCT k.failed_payments) * 1.00) / COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) >=0.4
                OR (COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) * 1.00) / COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) >=0.4)
            ORDER BY
                failed_payment_ratio DESC{code}

*fraud_profile_by_app_version*

{code:sql}SELECT
                 CAST(u.app_version AS varchar) || ':' || CAST(etl.country_code AS varchar) AS key,
                   COUNT(DISTINCT etl.user_id) AS count_of_users,
        COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.is_final_failed_payment THEN etl.order_id END) AS count_of_failed_payments,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.is_chargeback OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.order_id END) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
        (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.is_final_failed_payment THEN etl.order_id END) * 1.000)/ COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) AS failed_payment_ratio,
        (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.is_chargeback OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.order_id END) * 1.000)/ COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) AS fraud_payment_ratio
          FROM
              ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
                 LEFT JOIN glue.ng_pii.user_user AS u ON u.id=etl.user_id
          WHERE
              etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
            AND DATE_DIFF('day',u.created,etl.created) < 14
          GROUP BY
                  1
              HAVING
              COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) > 1
              AND COUNT(DISTINCT etl.user_id)>9{code}

{code:sql}SELECT x.key,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
SUM(x.price_eur) AS amount_of_in_app_orders,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_fraud_payments,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS fraud_payment_amount_ratio
FROM (
SELECT u.email || ':' || co.country_code AS key,
co.user_id AS user_id,
co.order_id AS order_id,
co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem OR co.is_chargeback OR co.uncovered_amount * 1.0 / NULLIF(co.capture_amount_total,0) > 0.5 THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payment
FROM glue.ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN glue.ng_pii.user_user u ON co.user_id = u.id 
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND co.order_type = 'food_delivery'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) AS x
WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 1
AND COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) > 1{code}

Hi [~accountid:61027984a539cb006846c64f], it seems that nothing has changed and such distant sales are still prohibited.

Below is the summary provided by an external counsel. Please let me know if you have any questions.

----

*The short answer is that none of the 3 product categories (vape liquids, salt without nicotine, e-cigarettes) are allowed to be sold via distance sale in Latvia.*

*A longer answer version would be the following.*

*The distance sale is prohibited by Article 8 para 2 of the* [*Law*|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/282077-on-the-handling-of-tobacco-products-herbal-products-for-smoking-electronic-smoking-devices-and-their-liquids] *which states:* *_“Tobacco products, electronic smoking devices, and refill containers may not be sold and purchased using a distance contract, including outside the territory of a European Union Member State or a state of the European Economic Area.”_*

*Now let’s assess whether vape liquids, salt without nicotine, e-cigarettes fall under this prohibition.*

+*_Vape liquids_*+

*Vape liquid is a liquid used in electronic smoking devices, which may or may not contain nicotine. Vape device is a device intended for a consumption of such liquid by allowing inhalation of a vapour* *of such liquid. Which of course is sold in containers e.g. cartridges, bottles etc.*

*Article 8 para 2 of the Law does not mention “vape liquid” literally. However, it mentions “refill containers” which is defined in Article 1 clause 8) as follows:*

*_“refill container is:_*

*_a) a refill container in which a nicotine-containing liquid is filled, and which can be used to refill an electronic cigarette;_*

*_b) a container in which a nicotine-free liquid is filled, and which can be used to refill an electronic smoking device;”_*

*Therefore, vape liquids fall under the distance sales ban. Such understanding has also been confirmed by unofficial opinion of the Health Inspectorate.*

+*_Salt without nicotine_*+

*I presume you mean the Salt smoking device containing nicotine free liquid. Pursuant to Article 1 clause 7), b) of the Law such device falls under the definition of electronic smoking device:*

*_b) electronic device which is a product or a component of that product, including a cartridge, a tank and the device without a cartridge or tank, which can be used for consumption of nicotine-free vapour via a mouthpiece and which can be disposable or refillable by means of a container which is filled with nicotine-free liquid, and a tank, or rechargeable with single use cartridges;_*

*Accordingly, it also falls under the distance sales ban as it has literally listed among the banned items.*

+*_e-cigarettes_*+

*Pursuant to Article 1 clause 7) a) and b) of the Law e-cigarettes fall under the definition of electronic smoking devices which fall under the distance sale ban.*

*As explained in our previous correspondence, there can be found quite a few websites on which many market participants offer to sell these kinds of products to the Latvian consumers. Nevertheless, it is not allowed and fine can be imposed in such cases. Pursuant to Article 14 para 8 of the Law, such fine for legal entities may range from EU 200 to EUR 700.*

*In case you have identified such violation, your can report them to State Revenue Service which supervises the compliance with these requirements.*

{code:sql}SELECT x.key,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
SUM(x.price_eur) AS amount_of_in_app_orders,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_fraud_payments,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS fraud_payment_amount_ratio
FROM (
SELECT json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.user.phone_country') || ':' || co.country_code AS key,
co.user_id AS user_id,
co.order_id AS order_id,
co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem OR co.is_chargeback OR co.is_final_failed_payment THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payment
FROM glue.ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN glue.archive_analytical.delivery_order_request d ON co.fraud_calculation_id = d.id  
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND co.order_type = 'food_delivery'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) AS x
WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 1
AND COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) > 1{code}

{code:sql} SELECT CAST (k.order_user_ip AS varchar) || ':' || CAST(k.country_code AS varchar) as key,
    COUNT(DISTINCT k.user_id) AS count_of_users,
            COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
            COUNT(DISTINCT k.failed_payments) AS count_of_failed_payments,
            COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
            (COUNT(DISTINCT k.failed_payments) * 1.00)/ COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) AS failed_payment_ratio,
            (COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) * 1.00)/ COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) AS fraud_payment_ratio 
            FROM
                (
                                        WITH inputs AS (
SELECT 
d.id AS calculation_id,
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.user.order_ip') AS order_ip
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request AS d
WHERE 
d.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
                SELECT DISTINCT i.order_ip AS order_user_ip, 
                etl.country_code AS country_code, etl.user_id AS user_id, etl.order_id AS order_id, 
                CASE WHEN etl.is_chargeback OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payments,
                CASE WHEN etl.is_final_failed_payment THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END AS failed_payments
                FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
                LEFT JOIN inputs AS i ON i.calculation_id = etl.fraud_calculation_id AND i.user_id = etl.user_id
                WHERE  etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'

                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)

                GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6

                1

                COUNT (DISTINCT k.order_id)

                OR

In addition to that we checked the requirements in the DPA 2018:

Within the first 21 days of each charge period a data controller must pay a charge to the Information Commissioner. Storing personal data (eg. storing invoices, contracts) is a processing activity which would qualify Bolt Operations UK limited as a data controller, nevertheless the there are some exemptions ([https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2018/9780111165782/schedule|https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2018/9780111165782/schedule|smart-link]), like

* for the purposes of matters of administration in relation to the members of staff and volunteers of, or persons working under any contract for services provided to, the data controller;
* for the purposes of advertising, marketing and public relations in respect of the data controller’s business, activity, goods or services;
* for the purposes of—
** *keeping accounts, or records of purchases, sales or other transactions,*
** deciding whether to accept any person as a customer or supplier, or
** making financial or financial management forecasts,

      in relation to any activity carried on by the data controller;

Based on the information that Bolt Operations UK limited is dormant (no business activity, no employees) I would assume that the only personal data processing process would be “*keeping accounts, or records of purchases, sales or other transactions”*.

{code:sql}SELECT 
CASE WHEN k.device_carrier_name = ' ' OR k.device_carrier_name is NULL THEN 'EMPTY'
                       ELSE CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(k.device_carrier_name, '[\\\\r\\\\n|]+', '-') AS varchar)
                       END || '::' ||
                   CASE
                       WHEN k.phone_check_carrier_name = ' ' OR k.phone_check_carrier_name is null THEN 'EMPTY_phone'
                       ELSE CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(phone_check_carrier_name, '[\\\\r\\\\n|]+', '-') AS varchar)
                       END || ':' || CAST(k.country_code AS varchar) as key,
  COUNT(DISTINCT k.user_id) AS count_of_users,
            COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
            COUNT(DISTINCT k.failed_payments) AS count_of_failed_payments,
            COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
            (COUNT(DISTINCT k.failed_payments) * 1.00)/ COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) AS failed_payment_ratio,
            (COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) * 1.00)/ COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) AS fraud_payment_ratio 
            FROM (
                                                    WITH inputs AS (
SELECT 
d.id AS calculation_id,
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.device_additional_info.carrier_name') AS device_carrier,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.phone_check.carrier_name') AS phone_carrier
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request AS d
WHERE 
d.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
)
                SELECT
                i.device_carrier AS device_carrier_name, 
                i.phone_carrier AS phone_check_carrier_name, 
                etl.country_code AS country_code, etl.user_id AS user_id, etl.order_id AS order_id, 
                CASE WHEN etl.is_chargeback OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payments,
                CASE WHEN etl.is_final_failed_payment THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END AS failed_payments
                FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
                LEFT JOIN inputs AS i ON i.calculation_id = etl.fraud_calculation_id AND i.user_id = etl.user_id
                WHERE  etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
                GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7
                ) AS k
            GROUP BY
                1
          HAVING
                COUNT (DISTINCT k.order_id)
                 > 10
               AND COUNT (DISTINCT k.user_id)
                 > 5
                AND ( 
               (COUNT(DISTINCT k.failed_payments) * 1.00 / COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) >=0.4)
                OR 
                (COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) * 1.00 / COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) >=0.4)
                )
            ORDER BY
                failed_payment_ratio DESC{code}

Доброго дня, Андрію,

Дякуємо за співпрацю та Ваші коментарі. Ми написали коментарі червоним кольором нижче, а також внесли невеликі редагування.

 

# Просимо змінити визначення в п 1.3, щоб було зрозуміло, що застраховані всі особи, які перебували в машині (за умови, що кількість пасажирів не перевищує кількість посадкових місць у машині) незалежно від того, хто замовив поїздку через сервіс Болт. Пропонуємо таке формулювання:

_Застрахована особа - фізична особа або особи (водій та пасажир(и)), які знаходяться у Забезпеченому ТС в момент ДТП, що сталося протягом поїздки, замовлення на яку було оформлено з використанням сервісу Bolt._

Також звертаємо увагу, що сервіс Bolt надає не Страхувальник, а його афільована особa Bolt Operations OU, тому правильніше скрізь писати сервіс Bolt, а не сервіс Страхувальника.

У нас у ДУ№3 (у вкладенні) вже було сформульоване коректне визначення Застрахованої особи, де вказані і водій і пасажири, які займають місця, призначені для сидіння згідно свідоцтва про державну реєстрацію ТЗ, незалежно від того, хто замовив поїздку. Пропоную просто там замінити «сервісу Страхувальника» на «сервісу Bolt» і тоді це буде виглядати так

«1.3. Вигодонабувач - фізична особа, яка може зазнати збитків в результаті настання страхового випадку. Застрахована особа - фізична особа - пасажир та водій забезпеченого транспортного засобу, замовлення на перевезення якого оформлене з використанням сервісу Страхувальника Bolt, та який на момент настання ДТП знаходився у цьому ТЗ та на законних підставах займав місце, призначене для сидіння згідно свідоцтва про державну реєстрацію ТЗ (включаючи водія). Застрахована особа вважається постраждалою, тільки якщо вона знаходилась в забезпеченому ТЗ та зазначена в довідці патрульної поліції щодо ДТП, як постраждала особа.»

Ми можемо також замінити "замовлення на перевезення якого" на "якщо замовлення на поїздку" без "якого"?

Справа в тому, що у нас замовлення на перевезення формально на 1 особу завжди (тобто замовник, наприклад, Іван), а насправді там може бути інша людина (не Іван) або декілька осіб.

Ми запропонували формулювання.

 

 

# Наразі у договорі прописано, що дані про поїздки мають бути у Додатку 1, а також мають передаватися Страхувальником окремо. Однак на практиці ми зараз не передаємо дані про поїздки, а лише (1) загальну їх кількість для розрахунку страхової премії та (2) інформацію про те, чи є наша поїздка в системі вже в процесі формування страхового випадку. Чи можемо ми навести положення з договором з відповідністю до того, що у нас на практиці?

Взагалі кажучи, Ви дійсно повинні пересилати нам Перелік з номерами поїздок по закінченню кожного кварталу. Ми це проговорювали ще до запуску цього проекту. Нам в ідеалі потрібен детальний Реєстр з повними даними по кожній поїздці (марка, модель, держ.номер авто, персональні дані водія та того, хто замовив поїздку та інше). Але ми домовились на компромісний варіант – пересилати нам Перелік тільки з унікальними номерами поїздок, які у свою чергу «зашифровують» всю іншу детальну інформацію по кожній поїздці. Цей пункт прибрати з договору не можна. Його потрібно залишити.

Ок.

 

# У договорі зазначено, що всі автомобілі повинні бути технічно справними, а водії повинні мати при собі права водія, інакше страхувальник має право відмовити у виплаті. На практиці ми повинні сказати, що через специфіку нашого бізнесу як платформи, а не традиційного таксопарку, у нас немає можливості перевіряти цю інформацію щодня. Ми вважаємо, що у будь-якому випадку ці обставини не повинні бути підставою для відмови у виплаті страхового відшкодування. Просимо виправити договір у цій частині.

Це наші стандартні фрази у п.1.16 Договору по такому виду страхування. Суть у тому, що автомобілі взагалі повинні експлуатуватися особами на законних підставах і бути технічно справними. Це просто основи ПДР України. На практиці ми постійно робимо страхові виплати вашим потерпілим пасажирам при ДТП без перевірки прав водія або технічної справності автомобіля. Але формально такий пункт у договорі повинен залишатися.

Ок.

 

# Також у договорі не зовсім зрозуміло, чи будуть страховим випадком такі ситуації:

(1) водій був у стані сп'яніння або іншим чином грубо порушив правила дорожнього руху

(2) водій перевозив дітей без спеціального крісла

(3) застраховані особи грубо порушили ПДР - не були пристебнуті ременем безпеки

Просимо вказати в договорі зрозуміліше, що навіть за таких обставин випадок вважається страховим.

В нашому договорі для вас такі випадки не є у переліку виключень зі страхових випадків. Ми на старті проекту їх прибрали. Хоча для інших партнерів зазвичай ці всі випадки є у переліку виключень зі страхових випадків. Тобто на практиці - по вашим випадкам ми просто не акцентуємо увагу на таких нюансах, і просто проводимо вашим клієнтам страхові виплати. Але явно вказувати у договорі, що ми будемо робити страхові виплати, якщо водій був п'яний та інше, ми теж не можемо.

На даний момент збільшувати ні пеню/штраф, ні терміни виплат (вони і так нині мінімально можливі) не можна. В ДУ№6 додали доповнення в п.13.12 "Зміни та доповнення до Договору можуть бути внесені тільки за взаємною згодою Страхувальника та Страховика, шляхом укладення додаткової угоди до діючого Договору."



8.              За лімітами страхових виплат просимо уточнити, чи залишилися % такими ж, якими вони були 2 роки тому, або змінилися у бік підвищення. Ми були б вдячні, якби у Вас була можливість їх трохи підвищити. В Таблиці травм всі % виплат по різним видам травм залишаються незмінними. Сама шкала % є стандартизованою страховою практикою (Континентальна шкала виплат).

Але у нас зараз підвищуються страхові суми в 2 рази по новій Додатковій угоді №6 (п.2). А це означає, що в абсолютних значеннях клієнти будуть отримувати в 2 рази більше страхових виплат.  Наприклад, якщо раніше виплата за перелом була 7000 грн, тепер буде 14000 грн.



9.             Щодо відповідальності Страховика за несвоєчасну виплату – просимо, крім пені у розмірі подвійної ставки НБУ, також передбачити штраф у розмірі 15% від невиплаченої суми. Ми розуміємо, що з Вами ми ще не мали таких випадків, але наша глобальна політика зобов'язує нас прописувати подібні штрафи по всіх країнах.

У нас зараз у договорі з вами прописані доволі стислі строки виплат – всього 10 днів. Хоча для всіх інших партнерів такий строк складає 30 дні. Зазвичай в подібних пунктах договорів передбачається або пеня, або штраф, а ніяк - і те і інше. Пеня - це більш справедливий інструмент відповідальності, тому що сума компенсації за затримку виплати тим більша, чим більший строк затримки.В договорі прописано виплату пені застрахованим у разі затримки виплати так: "12.3 Страховик несе майнову відповідальність за несвоєчасну виплату страхової виплати шляхом сплати одержувачу страхової виплати пені у розмірі 0,01% від суми страхової виплати за кожний день прострочення, але не більше ніж у розмірі підвійної облікової ставки НБУ за відповідний період." 

На даний момент збільшувати ні пеню/штраф, ні терміни виплат (вони і так нині мінімально можливі) не можна. Коли переможемо у війні, то можна буде повернутись до цього питання.

{code:sql}SELECT x.key,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
SUM(x.price_eur) AS amount_of_in_app_orders,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_fraud_payments,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS fraud_payment_amount_ratio
FROM (
SELECT json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.device_additional_info.net_wlan_bssid') || ':' || co.country_code AS KEY,
co.user_id AS user_id,
co.order_id AS order_id,
co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem OR co.is_chargeback OR co.is_final_failed_payment THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payment
FROM glue.ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN glue.archive_analytical.delivery_order_request d ON co.fraud_calculation_id = d.id  
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND co.order_type = 'food_delivery'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) AS x
WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 0{code}

I’ve confirmed this topic with Olatunde Olufowobi from the Commerce team and according to him the pre-authorisation release is usually instant from Bolt to payment provider, however it can take up to 14 days for the bank to release it back to the user’s account due to their internal processes.

30 days is the max amount of time banks can keep an authorization on hold without releasing it. This happens when certain providers have bugs and this is most common in Azerbaijan.

So the vast majority of cases should be instant and then at most 14 days to be released by the bank to the user’s account. In the most outlier cases, banks can take up to 30 days.

I’ll update the article to mention that the release can take up to 14 days but maintain that users should reach out to their bank because from our end the release is instant.

Thank you again for your request and I hope you have a great weekend\!

{code:sql}SELECT x.key,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
SUM(x.price_eur) AS amount_of_in_app_orders,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_fraud_payments,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS fraud_payment_amount_ratio
FROM (
SELECT json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.order.user_device_name') || '::' || substr(CAST(ROUND(CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.device_additional_info.storage_free_percentage') AS double),-1) AS varchar),1,2) || ':' || co.country_code AS KEY,
co.user_id AS user_id,
co.order_id AS order_id,
co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem OR co.is_chargeback OR co.is_final_failed_payment THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payment
FROM glue.ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN glue.archive_analytical.delivery_order_request d ON co.fraud_calculation_id = d.id  
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND co.order_type = 'food_delivery'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) AS x
WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 1{code}

{code:sql}  WITH avag_ride_price AS (
            SELECT etl.country_code, etl.city_id, avg(etl.partner_price) AS avg_price
            FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
                WHERE etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -10, current_date) as date)
   GROUP BY 1,2
            ),
            order1 AS (
            SELECT etl.order_id AS id, ot.driver_id AS driver_id, etl.card_alias AS card_aliAS
            FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
            JOIN glue.ng_public.company_order_try AS ot ON ot.order_id = etl.order_id AND ot.city_id = etl.city_id
            JOIN glue.ng_public.user_user u ON u.id = etl.user_id
            JOIN avag_ride_price ap ON ap.city_id = etl.city_id
             WHERE etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -10, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -10, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.state = 'finished'
            AND etl.partner_price > ap.avg_price * 3
            AND date_diff('day', u.created, etl.created) < 14
            GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
            ),
            order2 AS (
           SELECT etl.order_id AS id, ot.driver_id AS driver_id, etl.card_alias AS card_aliAS
            FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
            JOIN glue.ng_public.company_order_try AS ot ON ot.order_id = etl.order_id AND ot.city_id = etl.city_id
            JOIN glue.ng_public.user_user u ON u.id = etl.user_id
            JOIN avag_ride_price ap ON ap.city_id = etl.city_id
             WHERE etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -10, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -10, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.state = 'finished'
            AND etl.partner_price > ap.avg_price * 3
            AND date_diff('day', u.created, etl.created) < 14
            GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
            ),
            drivers AS
            (SELECT o1.driver_id AS driver_1, o1.card_aliAS AS card_aliAS, o2.driver_id AS driver_2
            FROM order1 AS o1
            JOIN order2 AS o2 ON o1.card_aliAS = o2.card_aliAS
            WHERE o1.id <> o2.id
            AND o1.driver_id <> o2.driver_id
            GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
            ),
            fraud_drivers AS (
            SELECT CAST(dd.driver_1 AS varchar)|| ',' || CAST(dd.driver_2 AS varchar) AS drivers, count(distinct dd.card_aliAS)
            FROM drivers AS dd
            GROUP BY 1
            HAVING COUNT(distinct dd.card_aliAS) > 1
            ),
            NS AS (
            SELECT 1 AS n
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 2
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 3
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 4
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 5
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 6
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 7
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 8
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 9
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 10
            ),
            final_drivers AS (
              SELECT TRIM(SPLIT_PART(d.drivers, ',', NS.n)) AS driver_id
            FROM NS AS NS
            --INNER JOIN fraud_drivers AS d ON NS.n <= regexp_match_count(d.drivers, ',') + 1
            GROUP BY 1

            ),
            sched_block AS (
            SELECT d.driver_id
            FROM final_drivers AS d
            JOIN glue.ng_public.fleet_driver_scheduled_blocking AS f ON d.driver_id = f.driver_id
            WHERE f."end" >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
            )
            SELECT CAST(etl.city_id AS varchar) || ':' || CAST(etl.order_id AS varchar) AS key,
            1 as cash_out_ride
            FROM final_drivers AS d
            JOIN glue.ng_public.fleet_driver AS f ON d.driver_id = f.id
            JOIN glue.ng_public.company_order_try AS ot ON ot.driver_id = d.driver_id
            JOIN ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl ON ot.city_id = etl.city_id AND ot.order_id = etl.order_id
            JOIN avag_ride_price ap ON ap.city_id = etl.city_id
            JOIN drivers AS df ON df.driver_1 = d.driver_id AND etl.card_alias = df.card_alias
            LEFT JOIN sched_block b ON b.driver_id = d.driver_id
             WHERE etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -10, current_date) as date)
                AND b.driver_id IS NULL
                AND f.status = 'active'
                AND etl.payment_state <> 'refunded'
                AND etl.partner_price > ap.avg_price * 3
            	AND ot.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -10, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.state = 'finished'
            GROUP BY 1  {code}

The Disciplinare di Gara was approved for the first time with the Determinazione Dirigenziale No. 4116 of September 8th, 2022 and published on the same day on the Albo Pretorio of the city, where it remained available for 15 days. Now it can only be found on the city’s historical portal of administrative acts, at this [link|http://www.comune.torino.it/giunta_comune/ricerca_internet]. However, only the main body of the Determinazione Dirigenziale can be downloaded, whereas its Allegato I (containing the Disciplinare) is not available anymore. 

However, we had stored that initial Disciplinare in our folders, so we can share it with you (attached). In this first version of it, as you can see, the maximum score for criteria 1 (presence in the surrounding municipalities) had been fixed at 20 points (5 points for each city covered)

On 12th September, a new Determinazione Dirigenziale (no. 4172, the one already linked in my memo) was adopted, and published the day after (13th September), to repeal the previous Determinazione in order to correct - as it reads - a material error in the Disciplinare. The new version of the latter therefore reduced from 20 to 16 the points for criteria 1 (therefore, 4 points for each surrounding city covered) and increased from 8 to 12 the points for criteria 2 (extension of the service area in the city of Turin)

This amendment got us very suspicious indeed. Though it gave us more hopes by reducing the score for the criterion we were not able to meet, we suspect that this decision from the city was made to facilitate some other operator which probably made some pressure on the city

*Step 1: Troubleshooting*

*⚠️* _Call the user (if not already on a call with them) to resolve the issue faster._

* Open the user's order in Admin Panel
* Ask the user if the [+brake warning light+|https://res.cloudinary.com/yourmechanic/image/upload/dpr_auto,f_auto,q_auto/v1/article_images/Press_Clutch_Brake_Pedal_Indicator_1_The_press_clutch_pedal_light_and_the_press_brake_pedal_light] on the car's dashboard is lit up:
** *_Yes:_* _Ask them to push the brake pedal while pushing and holding the start button to start the engine (if this helped, skip the rest of the process)_
** *_No:_* _Go to the next step_
* Ask the user if they see any other warning lights in the dashboard (if so, ask them to share a photo)
* Ask the user to go through the following steps together:
** Put the gear stick into the parking position (P)
** Press the brake pedal and try to start the engine using the keys or by pushing and holding the start button
** Put the gear stick into drive (D)
** (for vehicles with a manual parking brake) Ensure the parking brake is not on
** Try to move the vehicle carefully by pressing the gas pedal
* For BMW vehicles, see +Additional information on BMW electronic gearstick operation+
* If these steps didn't solve the issue, go to Step 2

*Step 2: Check for a blocked engine and reboot IoT*

* Check if you see an _Unblock engine_ button in the _Car actions_ section on the order page in Admin Panel:
** *_Yes:_* _The IoT might not unblock the engine correctly - click the Unblock engine and ask the user to try to start the engine again (if this helped, skip the rest of the process)_
** *_No:_* _Go to the next step_
* Reboot the vehicle's IoT and ask the user to wait for a few minutes before trying to turn the engine on again
* If this didn't help, go to Step 3

The desired logic is to prefer verification modal in case when app has data to present both, verification and campaigns modals. But as these modals are received from different endpoints, it is not always possible to guarantee this. So when app get campaigns modal, but verification modal is not received yet, app shows campaigns modal. And while campaigns modal is on screen, app can receive verification modal from backend - this should be the only case when campaigns modal is shown first, and verification modal is shown next.


We need to check these cases:

* verification modal is available from the very launch of the app (it’s present in the response from {{/mobility/appState/get/v1}}) and campaigns modal comes to the client with the first response from {{/comms/modal/list}}, and request to {{/comms/modal/list}} doesn’t take long time (<0.1 second)
* verification modal is available from the very launch of the app (it’s present in the response from {{/mobility/appState/get/v1}}) and campaigns modal comes to the client with the first response from {{/comms/modal/list}}, but request to {{/comms/modal/list}} takes a long time (>0.5 second)
* verification modal is not available from the very launch of the app (it’s not present in the response from {{/mobility/appState/get/v1}}), but it is present later in the response of {{/gateway/v1/getLocationConfig}} and campaigns modal comes to the client with the first response from {{/comms/modal/list}} and before the request to {{/gateway/v1/getLocationConfig}} is responded (i.e. campaigns modal arrives to client before verification modal)
* verification modal is not available from the very launch of the app (it’s not present in the response from {{/mobility/appState/get/v1}}), but it is present later in the response of {{/gateway/v1/getLocationConfig}} and campaigns modal comes to the client with the first response from {{/comms/modal/list}} but after the request to {{/gateway/v1/getLocationConfig}} is responded (i.e. campaigns modal arrives to client after verification modal)
* verification modal is not returned by {{/mobility/appState/get/v1}}, nor by {{/gateway/v1/getLocationConfig}}, but it is returned as part of the error on attempt to place a ride-hailing order (i.e. Barcelona compliance requirement of 15 minutes delay after accepting Terms & Conditions)

{code:sql}SELECT x.key,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_of_cash_orders,
SUM(x.price_eur) AS sum_of_cash_orders,
SUM(x.debt_eur) AS sum_of_debt,
(SUM(x.debt_eur) * 1.0) / SUM(x.price_eur) AS debt_sum_ratio
FROM (
SELECT co.country_code,
o.delivery_address || ':' || co.country_code AS key,
co.user_id AS user_id,
co.order_id AS order_id,
co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
co.uncovered_amount/NULLIF(co.eur_currency_rate,0) AS debt_eur
FROM glue.ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN glue.ng_delivery.delivery_order_order o ON co.order_id = o.id AND co.city_id = o.city_id
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND co.order_type = 'food_delivery'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'cash'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
HAVING co.uncovered_amount/NULLIF(co.eur_currency_rate,0) > 0.1
) AS x
WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) > 1
AND COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) > 1
AND SUM(x.debt_eur) > 0
AND (SUM(x.debt_eur) * 1.0) / SUM(x.price_eur) > 0.2
ORDER BY 6 DESC{code}

The way it works is that once the file and payslip is available on Immedis' side, the user will be able to see it in Workday when they type “my payslips”. The time when these become available should be on the Payperiod’s *Payroll Payment Date*. In case this is not visible, a ticket should be raised directly with Immedis somehow, so they can investigate this matter.

Note that there is no “Run” for payslips to become visible in Workday. Every time a user goes to “My Payslips” in workday, it will send out a request to the Immedis system, and will display everything that it can find. If it doesn’t find anything, and there is no “connection” error, then that means Immedis has not made it available yet.

Hope that this explains it a bit more.

{code:sql} WITH failed AS
                 (
                     SELECT bi.id AS id,
                            bi.country AS country,
                            bi.created AS          company_created,
                            bi.created AS          payment_created,
                            bi.balance / r.rate as amount_euro,
                            'failed' AS            payment_status
                     FROM glue.ng_public.business_invoicing_business_company AS bi
                              LEFT JOIN
                          glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON bi.currency = r.currency AND DATE (r.valid_on) = DATE (bi.created)
        WHERE
            bi.balance
            < 0
          AND bi.invoice_type='claim'
          AND bi.credit_limit=0
          AND bi.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
          AND bi.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
          )
            , other AS (      
        SELECT
            co.id AS id,
            co.country AS country,
            co.created AS company_created,
            p.created AS payment_created,
            pr.amount / r.rate AS amount_euro,
            CASE WHEN (ppr.state <> 'ignored') OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') THEN 'fraud' else p.state end as payment_status
        FROM
            glue.ng_public.business_business_company AS co
            JOIN
            glue.ng_public.payment_payment_user u ON u.external_id=co.id
            JOIN
            glue.ng_public.payment_payment_order po ON po.payment_user_id=u.id
            JOIN
            glue.ng_public.payment_payment as p ON p.payment_order_id = po.id
            JOIN
            glue.ng_public.payment_payment_row pr ON pr.id = p.last_payment_row_id
            LEFT JOIN
            glue.ng_public.fraud_user_latest_payment_problem as ppr ON ppr.payment_id = p.id
            LEFT JOIN
            glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON p.currency = r.currency AND DATE (r.valid_on) = DATE (p.created)
        WHERE
        co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
         AND co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
         AND u.type='business'
          AND p.state <> 'prepare'
          AND p.state <> 'created'
         AND po.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
         AND po.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
            AND p.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
          AND p.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
         AND pr.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
         AND pr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
          AND ppr.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
         AND ppr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
        GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
            ),
            payments AS (
        SELECT*
        FROM
            failed
        UNION ALL
        SELECT *
        FROM
            other
            ) 
        SELECT CAST(substr(u.email, position('@' in u.email) + 1) AS varchar) || ':' || CAST(o.country AS varchar) AS key,
                			COUNT (DISTINCT o.user_id) AS count_of_users,
                       		COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS count_of_companies,
                       		COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN  p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_companies_with_failed_payments,
                       		COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_companies_with_fraud_payments,
                      		( COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS failed_company_ratio,
                       		( COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS fraud_company_ratio
        FROM
            glue.ng_public.company_order o 
            JOIN payments AS p ON p.id= CAST(split_part(o.payment_method_id,'-',1) AS bigint)
            LEFT JOIN glue.ng_pii.user_user AS u ON u.id=o.user_id
        WHERE
            o.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
         AND o.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
         AND o.state = 'finished'
         AND o.payment_method_type = 'business'
        GROUP BY 1
        HAVING
            COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) >5
    AND ( 
    ((COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id)) > 0.3
            OR
     ((COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id)) > 0.3

*Results:*
Path that we draw consists of some number of circles which are recalculated based on the map zoom. Un fortunately, it’s not possible to use other google provided mechanisms (polyline, stamping) to achieve the same results. Thereby, we need to speed up heavy operations involved in path drawing:

# removing already drawn circles
# preparing an array of circles from which path consists
# drawing new circles

*Preparing an array of circles:*
currently we calculate circles for the whole path even if the small part of it is visible. It leads to heavy calculations which might obtain up to 20ms on main thread (iPhone 6s). The idea is to split path  into parts using visible bounding box and perform calculations and drawing only for them. This should reduce number of circles that should be removed and drawn in one time.

Here is some further background for you (which you can read more about in the incident log linked in the ticket): 

*Background*: 

* Fire occurred at warehouse in Gothenburg on 2 February 2022 and was reported at 2.32am. Cause is deemed to be a physically damaged battery box which was located outside of the warehouse under a roof that caught on fire which blew out the glass in the roof and damages walls around this are. Another fire was reported at 1.00pm on the same day which was caused by water leaking on electronic equipment due to a leak in the roof (caused by the first fire). 
* We have not received the police report as far as I am ware but am chasing to see what the conclusion was. 
* The landlord’s insurance is paying for the property damage and the insurance is in turn claiming that we shall pay this amount - which should be covered by our insurance. 
* We do not know how big the amount is yet. 

*Lease agreement*: 

* There is no specifics in the contract about property damage or similar and thus this is regulated by the applicable law. 
* Under SE law the tenant is responsible for damages to the property which are caused by the tenant, through the tenant’s carelessness or negligence. 
* In relation to damage caused by fire which was not caused by the tenant,  the tenant is only responsible for the damage if the tenant failed to exercise the required care and supervision of the premises. 
* It is up to the landlord to prove that the damage was cause by the tenant but the tenants liability is not removed by simply referring to the fact that it was an accident, that is not sufficient. Since I haven’t seen the police report it is difficult to assess how valid this claim is at this stage. 

*Insurance cover*: 

* Since we have an insurance which covers any property damage - any claim in relation to the above should be covered by our insurance company as far as I understand. It seems like you have some further insight into this so please let me know what would lead to the insurance not covering this claim? 
* The insurance company was informed of the fire straight away when it happened. 

*Additional legal advice*: 

* If we need additional information on the legal grounds for this claim we would have to engage external counsel to dig into the specifics in relation to fire protection regulations and whether this claim is valid and if we should contest the claim.
