{code:sql}SELECT x.key,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_of_cash_orders,
SUM(x.price_eur) AS sum_of_cash_orders,
SUM(x.debt_eur) AS sum_of_debt,
(SUM(x.debt_eur) * 1.0) / SUM(x.price_eur) AS debt_sum_ratio
FROM (
SELECT co.country_code,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.user.user_city') || '::' || json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.order.city_id') || ':' || co.country_code AS KEY,
co.user_id AS user_id,
co.order_id AS order_id,
co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
co.uncovered_amount/NULLIF(co.eur_currency_rate,0) AS debt_eur
FROM glue.ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN glue.archive_analytical.delivery_order_request d ON co.fraud_calculation_id = d.id  
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) AS date)

AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'cash'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
HAVING co.uncovered_amount/NULLIF(co.eur_currency_rate,0) > 0.1
) AS x
WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) > 1

{code:sql} SELECT
                                                     CAST(k.device_name AS varchar) || '::' || CAST(k.storage_free_percentage AS varchar) || ':' || CAST(k.country_code AS varchar) as key,                              
             COUNT(DISTINCT k.user_id) AS count_of_users,
            COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
            COUNT(DISTINCT k.failed_payments) AS count_of_failed_payments,
            COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
            (COUNT(DISTINCT k.failed_payments) * 1.00)/ COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) AS failed_payment_ratio,
            (COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) * 1.00)/ COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) AS fraud_payment_ratio
        FROM (
                                   WITH inputs AS (
SELECT 
d.id AS calculation_id,
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.device.name') AS device_name,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.device_additional_info.storage_free_percentage') AS storage_free_percentage
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request AS d
WHERE 
d.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
)
SELECT 
etl.order_id AS order_id, 
etl.user_id AS user_id,
etl.country_code AS country_code,
i.device_name AS device_name, 
ROUND(CAST(i.storage_free_percentage AS double),2) AS storage_free_percentage,
CASE WHEN etl.is_chargeback OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payments,
                CASE WHEN etl.is_final_failed_payment THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END AS failed_payments
          FROM
             ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
               LEFT JOIN inputs AS i ON i.calculation_id = etl.fraud_calculation_id AND i.user_id = etl.user_id
            WHERE
              etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
                GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7
                ) AS k
          GROUP BY
                  1    
              HAVING
              CAST(k.device_name AS varchar) || '::' || CAST(k.storage_free_percentage AS varchar) || ':' || CAST(k.country_code AS varchar) IS NOT NULL
              AND COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) > 1

            OR ((COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) * 1.00)/ COUNT(DISTINCT k.order_id) > 0.3)
            ) 
          ORDER BY
                   failed_payment_ratio DESC

Hi, Kristjan\!

Yes, the Omnibus directive foresees a phone number, however, we decided that we will not provide one (having different numbers for different verticals in different countries seemed unreasonable) based on [ECJ’s Amazon decision|https://www.stevens-bolton.com/site/insights/articles/ecj-on-contact-information-obligations-of-online-traders] according to which _if online CS is adequate and sufficient, vendors can add CS channel instead of phone._

_It was held by the ECJ that traders are not obliged to provide their telephone number in “all circumstances”. Rather, the ECJ found under the CRD, the scope of “where available” to mean that traders only needed to provide such information, where those means of communicating already exist. Whilst the ECJ recognised the requirement for traders to provide means of communication that enable the consumer to contact the trader quickly and efficiently, it noted that this does not prevent traders from providing other alternative means of communication – such as call-back services._

About other means of communication - it isn’t durable medium, however, I hope this is enough - we added to our Client T&Cs the following clause: The Client can contact Bolt’s customer support via chat function on the Bolt Food Platform where the Client can review the open chats and the communication history thereof, including its date and time, for 6 months as of creating the chat.

Let’s explain that we have two ways to contact Bolt - we have the e-mail as well as the chat function - and see whether this is sufficient for them.

Kind regards

Marilin

{code:sql}        WITH failed AS
                 (
                     SELECT bi.id,
                            bi.country,
                            bi.created AS          company_created,
                            bi.created AS          payment_created,
                            bi.balance / r.rate AS amount_euro,
                            'failed' AS            payment_status
                     FROM glue.ng_public.business_invoicing_business_company bi
                              LEFT JOIN
                          glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON bi.currency = r.currency AND DATE (r.valid_on) = DATE (bi.created)
        WHERE
            bi.balance
            < 0
          and bi.invoice_type='claim'
          and bi.credit_limit=0
          AND bi.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -90, current_date) as date)
          AND bi.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -100, current_date) as date)
            )
            , other AS
            (
        SELECT
            co.id,
            co.country,
            co.created AS company_created,
            p.created AS payment_created,
            pr.amount / r.rate as amount_euro,
            CASE WHEN (ppr.state <> 'ignored') OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') THEN 'fraud' else p.state end as payment_status
        FROM
            glue.ng_public.business_business_company as co
            JOIN
            glue.ng_public.payment_payment_user u on u.external_id=co.id
            JOIN
            glue.ng_public.payment_payment_order po on po.payment_user_id=u.id
            JOIN
            glue.ng_public.payment_payment as p ON p.payment_order_id = po.id
            JOIN
            glue.ng_public.payment_payment_row pr ON pr.id = p.last_payment_row_id
            LEFT JOIN
            glue.ng_public.fraud_user_latest_payment_problem as ppr ON ppr.payment_id = p.id
            LEFT JOIN
            glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON p.currency = r.currency AND DATE (r.valid_on) = DATE (p.created)
        where p.created > CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -90, current_date)as date)
        AND co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -100, current_date) as date)
        AND u.type='business'
          AND p.state <> 'prepare'
          AND p.state <> 'created'
          AND po.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -90, current_date) as date)
         AND po.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -100, current_date) as date)
            AND p.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -90, current_date) as date)
          AND p.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -100, current_date) as date)
         AND pr.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -90, current_date) as date)
         AND pr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -100, current_date) as date)
          AND ppr.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -90, current_date) as date)
         AND ppr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -100, current_date) as date)
        GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
            ),
            payments AS
            (
        SELECT*
        FROM
            failed
        union all
        SELECT *
        FROM
            other
            )
        SELECT cast(pmu.card_bin as varchar) || ':' || cast(o.country as varchar) as key,
                       	COUNT (DISTINCT o.user_id) as count_of_users,
                       	COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS count_of_companies,
                       	COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_companies_with_failed_payments,
                       	COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_companies_with_fraud_payments,
                      	(COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN  p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS failed_company_ratio,
                       	(COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' then p.id else null end) * 1.0)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS fraud_company_ratio
        FROM
            glue.ng_public.company_order o
            join payments p ON p.id= CAST(split_part(o.payment_method_id,'-',1) AS bigint)
            JOIN
            glue.ng_public.payment_payment_user u ON u.external_id=p.id
            JOIN
            glue.ng_public.payment_payment_method_user pmu ON pmu.payment_user_id=u.id
        WHERE
            o.created > CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -90, current_date) as date)
            AND o.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -100, current_date) as date)
            AND o.state = 'finished'
            AND o.payment_method_type = 'business'
        GROUP BY 1
        HAVING COUNT (DISTINCT p.id)
             >5
           AND ( 
           ((COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id))
             > 0.2
            or
             (( COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id))
             > 0.2){code}

Hi [~accountid:61c1e05b90cfd200714bc0a7], we could send bulk email with an amendment attached, however we need the signature from each separate partner in order to increase commission, because unilateral increase is not allowed under our terms.

This question was also answered in our Confluence page re the contracts with partners - [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3918790850/FAQ+-+Contracts+with+partners+restaurants+in+Eastern+Europe+UA+and+AZ|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3918790850/FAQ+-+Contracts+with+partners+restaurants+in+Eastern+Europe+UA+and+AZ|smart-link]

The answer is as follows:

*_We want to change (increase) the commission for the parter, but they disagree / do not react and do not sign the addendum. How can we push them? Can we just continue with change?_* 
_In order to change commission an addendum needs to be signed. Consent to new commission needs to be formalised as addendum, tacit consent is not enough. If the restaurant does not sign the addendum, we need to persuade them._
_How to persuade? Basically there're 2 incentives - positive and negative._
_- Positive: agree some benefit with the restaurant in exchange for signing the addendum with new commission. It can be marketing campaign, free tablet, etc._
_- Negative: threaten that if the parter doesn't sign an addendum by X date, we'll send them a termination notice for convenience (see below) and kick them out of the platform._
_In the second case we should be ready to accept that this may ruin our relationship with the partner, since we put the question point-blank._

*order_fraud_driver_high_frequency_cash_ride*

{code:sql}WITH ot_convert_timezone AS (          
            SELECT DISTINCT
                DATE_ADD('hour', timezone_hour(at_timezone(ot.created, sc.timezone)), ot.created) AS local_ot_created,
               etl.order_id,
                etl.city_id,
                ot.driver_id,
                etl.partner_price,
                etl.user_price
                FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
                JOIN ng_public.company_order_try ot ON etl.order_id = ot.order_id AND etl.city_id = ot.city_id
                LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_city AS sc ON sc.id = etl.city_id
                WHERE etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.payment_method_group = 'cash'
                AND etl.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND etl.city_id NOT IN (993,997,991,1167)
                 AND ot.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -1, current_date) as date)
                AND ot.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -1, current_date) as date)
                 AND ot.state = 'finished'
            ),
            hourly_data AS ( 
            SELECT	
                etl.period_local AS local_hour,
                etl.driver_id,
                sc.name AS city_name,
                sc.country_code,
                sc1.name AS country_name,
                sc1.zone,
                etl.finished_orders AS hourly_finished_orders, 
                --etl.has_order_minutes + etl.waiting_for_orders_minutes AS total_busy_minutes,
                ROUND(etl.finished_orders/(etl.has_order_minutes + etl.waiting_for_orders_minutes)*15, 0) AS no_order_fifteen,
                ROUND(etl.finished_orders/(etl.has_order_minutes + etl.waiting_for_orders_minutes)*30, 0) AS no_order_thirty,
                COUNT(DISTINCT ot.order_id) AS hourly_finished_cash_orders,
                ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT ot.order_id)/(etl.has_order_minutes + etl.waiting_for_orders_minutes)*15, 0)AS no_cash_order_fifteen,
                ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT ot.order_id)/(etl.has_order_minutes + etl.waiting_for_orders_minutes)*30, 0) AS no_cash_order_thirty
            FROM
                glue.ng_public.etl_driver_hourly_activity AS etl
                LEFT JOIN ot_convert_timezone AS ot
                    ON etl.driver_id = ot.driver_id
                    AND etl.period_local = DATE_TRUNC('hour', ot.local_ot_created)
                LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_city AS sc
                    ON sc.id = etl.city_id
                LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_country AS sc1
                    ON sc.country_code = sc1.code
            WHERE
                CAST(etl.period_local AS date) between CAST(DATE_ADD('week', -1, current_date) as date) AND CURRENT_DATE
                AND (etl.has_order_minutes > 0 OR etl.waiting_for_orders_minutes > 0)
                AND sc.id NOT IN (993,997,991,1167)
            GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,etl.has_order_minutes,etl.waiting_for_orders_minutes
            ),
            target_date AS (
            SELECT 
                DATE(hd.local_hour) AS local_date, 
                hd.zone, 
                hd.driver_id, 
                MAX(hd.hourly_finished_cash_orders) AS max_hourly_finished_cash_orders,
                MAX(hd.no_cash_order_fifteen) AS max_no_cash_order_fifteen,
                MAX(hd.no_cash_order_thirty) AS max_no_cash_order_thirty
            FROM 
                hourly_data AS hd 
            WHERE 	
                hd.zone <> 'we'
            GROUP BY 1,2,3
            HAVING MAX(hd.hourly_finished_cash_orders) > 6 AND MAX(hd.no_cash_order_fifteen) > 5
            )
            SELECT DISTINCT 
                CAST(ot.city_id AS varchar) ||':'|| CAST(ot.order_id AS varchar) AS key, 
                1 AS fraud_high_frequency_cash_ride
            FROM 
                target_date AS td 
                LEFT JOIN ot_convert_timezone AS ot
                    ON ot.driver_id = td.driver_id 
                    AND DATE(local_ot_created) = td.local_date{code}

*I used h3 version 4.0.0 beta in this notebook.*

General approach:

# Split the polygon into h3 cells
# Define affinity between h3 cells as a function of the distance between their centres and the number of orders where driver is in one cell and goes for pickup to another
# Recursively split in halves until every cluster has less orders per minute than the target number

Spectral clustering was chosen because it has both the ability to select the number of clusters (I needed 2), and to implement a custom affinity matrix (I needed to introduce cross-cell pickups)

The downsides of the prototype are:

* It failed to draw polygons around Thames (I picked London because (1) it was big (2) it has a river that’s hard to cross in some areas, so clusters shouldn’t intersect it where there are no bridges)
* The result is not particularly even by orders: some clusters could be merged
* I take overall orders per minute while in practice peaks might not happen at the same time

I added Georgia to the Privacy memo. As long as it is just a selfie, it would not be biometric data (also not under GDPR). But if you do specific technical processing relating to the  characteristics of a natural person (eg. facial characteristics), which allow or confirm the unique identification of that natural person, than it is “biometric data”

Definition of *Biometric (Georgian Privacy Law)*: *“*Any physical, mental, or behavioural feature which is unique and constant for each natural person and which can be used to identify this person (fingerprints, footprints, iris, retina (retinal image), *facial features*).” Biometric data is also considered as *Special category data.* 

The Georgian Data Protection Authority published guidelines about on the processing biometric data (not available in english)[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SI-uMYS-HDpX-kz1twJ3aD79N1HbqQcF/view?usp=sharing|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SI-uMYS-HDpX-kz1twJ3aD79N1HbqQcF/view?usp=sharing|smart-link] Maybe Georgian Ops can assist translating the “Guidelines”

We’ll keep monitoring, but we expect that fraud will be severely reduced after these actions.

We can confirm the observations on the Memo is right, under S.56 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015, we are required to refund any sums owed to our passengers back to their original payment method, unless that passenger expressly agrees to accept a different payment method. Our current method of partial refunds back to Bolt Balance is therefore illegal in the UK.

A key solution to mitigate against this, would be for us to give passengers a choice for their allocated refunds to either go to their Bolt Balance account or back to their bank account. If they don't want it in their BB account we need to honour that and send it back to their bank account (as the law requires).

From a legal perspective, it is irrelevant if Bolt’s current technical processes make this difficult or not possible to do. Failure to comply may result in fines issued to Bolt from consumer regulators, passengers may challenge their contracts with us and (as already discussed) ongoing problems may arise with TfL and other transport regulators if complaints are consistent. I'm just looking into the full scale of repercussions - but please consider the above in the interim.

I’m just in the process of looking into how we can quantify the risk if we continue down this path of operation, for example what kind of fines we may receive from a regulator, risks from passenger complaints and how this could compromise our position with the regulator. {code:sql}WITH failed as (
 SELECT bi.id,
        bi.country,
        bi.created AS company_created,
        bi.created AS payment_created,
        bi.balance / r.rate as amount_euro,
        'failed' AS payment_status
 FROM glue.ng_public.business_invoicing_business_company bi
 LEFT join glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON bi.currency = r.currency AND DATE (r.valid_on) = DATE (bi.created)
 WHERE
   bi.balance < 0
  AND bi.invoice_type = 'claim'
  AND bi.credit_limit = 0
  AND bi.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND bi.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
 ), other AS (
 SELECT
    co.id,
    co.country,
    co.created AS company_created,
    p.created AS payment_created,
    pr.amount / r.rate AS amount_euro,
    CASE WHEN (ppr.state <> 'ignored') OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') THEN 'fraud' else p.state end as payment_status
FROM
    glue.ng_public.business_business_company co
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment_user u ON u.external_id=co.id AND u.type='business'
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment_order po ON po.payment_user_id=u.id
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment as p ON p.payment_order_id = po.id
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment_row pr ON pr.id = p.last_payment_row_id
    LEFT JOIN
    glue.ng_public.fraud_user_latest_payment_problem as ppr ON ppr.payment_id = p.id
    LEFT JOIN
    glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON p.currency = r.currency AND DATE (r.valid_on) = DATE (p.created)
WHERE
  co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND p.state <> 'prepare'
  AND p.state <> 'created'
  AND u.type='business'
  AND po.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND po.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND p.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND p.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND pr.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND pr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND ppr.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND ppr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
payments AS (
select *
FROM
    failed
UNION
SELECT *
from other
),
inputs AS (
SELECT 
d.id AS calculation_id,
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.device_additional_info.device_fingerprint') AS device_fingerprint
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request AS d
WHERE 
d.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
SELECT CAST(i.device_fingerprint AS varchar) || ':' || cast(o.country as varchar) as key,
		COUNT (DISTINCT o.user_id) AS count_of_users,
		COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS count_of_companies,
		COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_companies_with_failed_payments,
		COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_companies_with_fraud_payments,
		(COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN  p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS failed_company_ratio,
		(COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' then p.id else null end) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS fraud_company_ratio
FROM
    glue.ng_public.company_order o
join 
payments p ON p.id = cast(split_part(o.payment_method_id,'-',1) as bigint)
JOIN inputs AS i ON i.order_id = o.search_token AND i.user_id = o.user_id 
where
	o.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
	AND o.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
	AND o.state = 'finished'
    AND o.payment_method_type = 'business'
GROUP BY 1
HAVING COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) > 5
   AND (
   (( COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id)) > 0.3
or
 (( COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id)) >  0.3

Hey [~accountid:60afc00fb0b5600069b1bd49] the source of the discrepancy is because you’re comparing 2 different values.

In the tax report I assume you’re taking the first measure - Total Finished Trip Payments which is the sum of ride price if the order is status = finished.

Now in the tax report I believe you check the {{Ingresos Brutos (incluye la cuota de Bolt)}} which translated is Total Gross Fares. Now they might sound similar but the calculation is slightly different:

total gross fares = total finished trip payments - toll road fees - booking fees 

which can be easily calculated using the tax report: 17,079.25 (gross fares) + 8.20 (toll) + 0.00 (booking fees) = 17087.45 (total finished trip payments).

Let me know if this is clear or you have any questions

Retrained a text-field detection model including V1 paper version.

Don’t have text GTs so can’t measure accuracy but only coverage.

It seems that simply swapping the bbox model as is makes the HRFR a lot worse, from 38% to 51% (using the threshold used for V11, aka 0.6). The reason is that the new bbox model is not rotation sensitive, e.g. bboxes are detected even if the doc is wrongly rotated, which triggers [this|https://github.com/bolteu/data-science/blob/master/sagemaker-jenkins/ocr/src/ocr/base_class.py#L137] condition. No more rotations are tried, given all bboxes are detected but the OCR fails to read rotated text (*Google OCR actually does a pretty good job at this regardless of rotation!*). So I commented out the {{if len(bboxes) == len(results):}} condition (essentially not stopping necessarily when all bboxes get detected, but giving it more rotation chances to fix the empty fields) and HRFR massively improves to 24%.

Shall we deploy the change then (e.g. new bbox model + removing the {{if len(bboxes) == len(results):}} condition)?

👍 *Pros*

* decrease in HRFR for KE DL V1 (unknown accuracy impact)

👎 *Cons*

* 9% increase in [latency|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4109697739/OCR+experiments#Allowing-more-rotations]
* unknown effect on other documents. In theory the effect is minimal and it applies only when documents are not captured straight. Is it worth it? *Probably not for just one version of one document*. Also, Google OCR seems to be able to read text even when rotated, so detecting bboxes should be sufficient?

Still keep this in mind for future potential improvements

As this MSA clause would apply for all SOW’s (already signed and the ones to be signed in the future), then the date inclusion is not the best option. I propose to have it as follows:

_Effective as of twelve (12) months as of the Effective Date of each Statement of Work, the Supplier shall have the right to annually increase the fees for the Services which were valid on 31st of December of the previous year by change in annual consumer price index (for all urban areas) as published by Statistics South Africa for that previous year, but not more than 3%. Everything that exceeds this stated threshold, requires mutual agreement between the Parties._

BTW, in the valid Oaksure SLA, we have already cl 2.6.2.5, which basically allows us to increase the prices up to 5% annually. This seems worse for Bolt than proposed by the MSA clause above. In principle, as this MSA clause overrides the SLA, then basically, if Oaksure agrees, we are now agreeing upon a trackable, but also more favourable mechanism for Bolt.

In practice, as I see this clause to apply to existing SLA as follows: Oaksure has the right to increase the fees that were valid on 31.12.2022 after 01.02.2023 1x annually by 2022 ZA annual urban areas CPI (but not more than 3%).

To balance this price increase, both of the parties may terminate the SLA that we have now in place for convenience by providing 45 days written notice of such termination to the other party (cl 3.2). For future SOW, our MSA foresees (cl 14.2) that both parties may terminate the SOW for convenience by providing 90 days written notice of such termination to the other party (if not agreed otherwise in that new SOW).

I have reviewed the contract and have added some initial questions and comments below: 

*Questions*: 

* What is the total/ annual/ monthly contract value of this agreement?

* *Clause 6*: we do not want to issue any surety and if this would be requested we would need to know before entering into the agreement whether such surety shall be provided. Can they make this assessment now already so we know their assessment? 
* *Clause 7*: invoicing should be specified so we can ensure that we receive the invoice via e-mail and not only in physical mail. Are you comfortable with the 30 days invoicing period? As far as I am aware we are not always able to meet this deadline due to internal accounting processes. 
* *Clause 8*: 
** We can't enter into a contract that is valid from 1 september 2022 since our car sharing business was not in place at that point yet and we don't enter into contracts that will be applicable retroactively. Starting date to be amended to an upcoming date. 
** Contract includes an automatic extension of 1 year: extension should be changed to only be applied if it is agreed in writing by both parties at least 3 months before the end date. 
** Generally we like to enter into contracts until further notice but with a reasonable notice period such as 3 months. Please assess if this could be applied here as well from a commercial perspective. 
* *Clause 9*: Insufficient confidentiality clause which does not properly define what confidential information is covered and does not include a survival period. The survival period should be 3-5 years. 
* *Clause 12*: Liability limitation also needs to be included for Bolt. Currently our liability is unlimited, it needs to be clearly stated that we cannot be held liable for indirect damages and loss and that our general liability is capped at the contract value. 
* *Clause 14*: The contract includes wording that provides Circle K with the option of transferring the agreement to any other party without the approval of Bolt. Generally this means that we can be in a position where we have a contract that is valid for 1 year with another party without approving such party. This wording needs to be excluded. We can accept that Circle K can transfer or assign the agreement to any other party within the same group and the same transfer right should also be provided to Bolt for any company within the same group. 
* *New clause*: Since they also want to apply their terms and conditions we should include some wording on the priority of these separate terms since the terms otherwise will contradict each other and we should clarify that unless agreed otherwise in the agreement the terms and conditions shall apply.

* *Clause 3.2*: Circle K cannot guarantee that the portal is available to us at all times. We should at least include some form of minimum standard here since currently Circle K cannot be held responsible at all even if the portal isn't available during a longer period of time.

Thank you for the clarification! I think there are 3 scenarios here that should be addressed:

# Contractual penalty is applied (in accordance with TnC-s). For an example - car is left dirty, fuel tank empty etc. This would be the first scenario. How can the user contest the penalty? How can they see the evidence/circumstances based on what the penalty was issued? As most of Bolt Drive users are customers (as defined by the law), we should keep that in mind: if the user receives this notice is this enough to apply the penalties? Or should we provide additional information?
## As the fines are paid directly to Bolt or its subsidiary and this is not an automated decision making, I’d guess the personal data processing impacts would be manageable. [~accountid:61b0698dfe9f3000680f0585] - what is your opinion? 
# Damages/fines are applied - the car gets scratched or the car was impounded by the police. In that scenario (second one) we are not operating in accordance with the TnCs and list of penalties, but rather the actual costs that was paid. This means that we should be able to provide evidence that we have suffered damages and based on the location - our burden of proof can vary a great deal. Poking [~accountid:61b0698dfe9f3000680f0585] - from personal data processing point-of-view: should the user have the option to pay the parking/speeding fines themself?
## We have had different scenarios how the damages are handled - from paying right away, from reducing the amount claimed, ending with a payment schedule for massive damages. What I am saying - it is more likely that damages cannot be handled via pop-up notification and uploading a proof of payment, rather it is a manual process. Tho, the user should be notified that some process is ongoing regarding their activities.
# Hybrid (penalty + damages) - for an example: causing an accident while under the influence. This should be either broken into two different parts (penalty - that could be processed in-app) and damages (that might fall under different regulations).

Hey!

This seems to be pan-European regulation, regarding the temperature fluctuation/deviations: 

[https://eur-lex.europa.eu/EN/legal-content/summary/quick-frozen-food.html|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/EN/legal-content/summary/quick-frozen-food.html|smart-link]

[https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A01989L0108-20130701|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A01989L0108-20130701|smart-link] 

And this is directly implemented in Lithuania:

# For quick-frozen foods, the temperature must be kept constant at minus 18 C or below in all areas of the product. A short-term temperature rise of up to 3 C is allowed during transport.
# Temperature variations of the product during local distribution and in retail display cabinets must not exceed 3 C.

[https://www.e-tar.lt/portal/lt/legalAct/TAR.05BF4E3347BB/asr|https://www.e-tar.lt/portal/lt/legalAct/TAR.05BF4E3347BB/asr|smart-link]

Looks like this 3 degree variation is also applicable here. 

This means we have several approaches here to be compliant. On the whole, larger mass items should not cause us worry, but smaller items, like single ice cream, could:

→ We calculate the minimum mass of the frozen product that could be set ready for the delivery;

→ We use thermal bags for prolonging the thawing.

→ The bags ready for delivery are kept in a cool place (+4’C)
There’s no agreement we should continue with FE changes.

We talking about a potential notification requirement for the processing of unique identifiers. So, the [Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013|https://www.gov.za/documents/protection-personal-information-act] (POPIA) requires responsible parties to obtain prior authorization from the Information Regulator to process personal information in certain circumstances, including:

* When processing data subject *unique identifiers* for:
** a purpose different from the collection purpose; *and*
** to link the information with information held by other responsible parties.

If that would be the case, than a controller may not carry out information processing that has been notified to the Regulator until the Regulator has completed its investigation or until there is a notice that a more detailed investigation will not be conducted (4 weeks deadline for the regulator for the notice, 13 weeks for the more detailed investigation). Failure to notify pocessing subject to prior authorisation is an offence (Penalty set out in sec 107)

The [guidance note |https://inforegulator.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/InfoRegSA-GuidanceNote-PriorAuthorisation-20210311-1.pdf]is not providing any more information about the processing of unique identifiers (3.1.1. of the guidance note)

_2.8. “Unique Identifier”, as defined in POPIA, means any identifier that is assigned to a data subject and is used by a responsible party for the purposes of the operations of that responsible party and that uniquely identifies that data subject in relation to that responsible party”._

_3.1. In accordance with section 58(1) of POPIA and subject to section 57(3) of POPIA, the responsible party must notify the Regulator that he, she or it is processing or intends to process any of the following personal information, as referred to in section 57(1) of POPIA-_

_3.1.1. Unique identifiers of data subjects for_ *_a purpose other than the one for which the identifier was specifically intended at collection_*_; and with the aim of_ *_linking the information together with information processed by other responsible parties_*_;_

_➢ Examples of unique identifier are, amongst others- Bank Account Numbers or any account number; Policy Number;_ *_Identity Number;_* _Employee Number; Student Number; Telephone or cell phone number; or Reference Number._

There are 2 main requirements:
1) *_purpose other than the one for which the identifier was specifically intended at collection_*
2)l*_inking the information together with information processed by other responsible parties_*

In my opinion by using SmileID to check the ID of drivers we are linking the ID (“Unique Identifier”) with additional information processed by other responsible parties (The ID is linked with the information from the government data base the the ID is valid) BUT I am not sure about the 1st requirement. We are collecting the ID and ID number for the main purpose of verifying the driver, or are there other purposes as well. If the verification process is the *_purpose for which the identifier was specifically intended at collection a notification would not be necessary. What is your legal opinion on that?_*

1️⃣ The non-OK responses rule is working out of the box for us (as with any other common rule in our alerting system). 

However, it has one important limitation: it measures the number of errors per the whole backend endpoint, not per particular {{model_id}}. E.g. for all OCR models, we call {{internal/ocr/getPrediction}} endpoint with the parameter {{model_id}}. We won’t learn from this alert that for particular model_id, the number of errors has increased significantly IF it doesn’t increase significantly for all OCR model ids. 

On the other hand, the number of requests is small for now (<10 per minute), so it might be enough for us so far.

I checked if we can remove the booking_uuid from our systems. It us currently used in the following cases:

* on {{client/checkoutCompleteAnalyticsService}} to  determine the paymentMethod → this part will be removed entirely from order side as part of the refactoring analytics service project
* on AdminService → {{internal/getOrderDetails}}, {{internal/createCashAdjustements}} & {{adminPanel/order/get}}
** it is part of the userBaskets field
** in AdminPanel it is used to get fraudData details for an order; however to get that data we also use {{user_basket_auth_id}} when booking_uuid is not available; -the good news is that- {{user_basket_auth_id}} -is always not null in our DB (user-basket db schema shows that it can also be null, but I ran a query on the current data and it returns that there are no null values in our table; furthermore, there was a recent task- [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/FDO-3537|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/FDO-3537|smart-link] -that made sure we do not accept null values on order creation.- → -we can use- {{user_basket_auth_id}} -as the only field for fetching fraud_data-
** {{user_basket_auth_id}} is -1 for all business orders {{FAKE_BUSINESS_DELIVERY_USER_BASKET_AUTH_ID}} ; however, for these orders, {{booking_uuid}} is also null → no issues here
* on invoicing service:
** {{internal/getOrderDataForTransaction}} → from node-monitor it seems to not be in use anymore [http://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/u5KFgwyZk/delivery-order-invoicing-monitor?orgId=1&refresh=1m|http://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/u5KFgwyZk/delivery-order-invoicing-monitor?orgId=1&refresh=1m]
** {{internal/getOrderTransactions}} → part of userBaskets details along with {{user_basket_auth_id}} which is not null

My conclusion is that we can safely remove {{booking_uuid}} from our codebase since we have {{user_basket_auth_id}} which is not null for all user-baskets and can be used as an alternative identifier ({color:#bf2600}-should drop the null option from db-schema-{color})

{code:sql} WITH failed as (
 SELECT bi.id,
        bi.country,
        bi.created AS company_created,
        bi.created AS payment_created,
        bi.balance / r.rate as amount_euro,
        'failed' AS payment_status
 FROM glue.ng_public.business_invoicing_business_company bi
 LEFT join glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON bi.currency = r.currency AND DATE (r.valid_on) = DATE (bi.created)
 WHERE
   bi.balance < 0
  AND bi.invoice_type = 'claim'
  AND bi.credit_limit = 0
  AND bi.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND bi.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
 ), other AS (
 SELECT
    co.id,
    co.country,
    co.created AS company_created,
    p.created AS payment_created,
    pr.amount / r.rate AS amount_euro,
    CASE WHEN (ppr.state <> 'ignored') OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') THEN 'fraud' else p.state end as payment_status
FROM
    glue.ng_public.business_business_company co
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment_user u ON u.external_id=co.id AND u.type='business'
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment_order po ON po.payment_user_id=u.id
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment as p ON p.payment_order_id = po.id
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment_row pr ON pr.id = p.last_payment_row_id
    LEFT JOIN
    glue.ng_public.fraud_user_latest_payment_problem as ppr ON ppr.payment_id = p.id
    LEFT JOIN
    glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON p.currency = r.currency AND DATE (r.valid_on) = DATE (p.created)
WHERE
  co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND p.state <> 'prepare'
  AND p.state <> 'created'
  AND u.type='business'
  AND po.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND po.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND p.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND p.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND pr.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND pr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND ppr.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND ppr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
payments AS (
select *
FROM
    failed
UNION
SELECT *
from other
),
inputs AS (
SELECT 
d.id AS calculation_id,
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.user.creation_ip') AS creation_ip
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request AS d
WHERE 
d.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
SELECT CAST(i.creation_ip AS varchar) || ':' || cast(o.country as varchar) as key,
		COUNT (DISTINCT o.user_id) AS count_of_users,
		COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS count_of_companies,
		COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_companies_with_failed_payments,
		COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_companies_with_fraud_payments,
		(COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN  p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS failed_company_ratio,
		(COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' then p.id else null end) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS fraud_company_ratio
FROM
    glue.ng_public.company_order o
join 
payments p ON p.id = cast(split_part(o.payment_method_id,'-',1) as bigint)
JOIN inputs AS i ON i.order_id = o.search_token AND i.user_id = o.user_id 
where
	o.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
	AND o.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
	AND o.state = 'finished'
    AND o.payment_method_type = 'business'
GROUP BY 1
HAVING COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) > 5
   AND (
   (( COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id)) > 0.3
or
 (( COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id)) >  0.3
 ){code}

Hi [~accountid:6299f17a9582b8006fc6b6c8] and [~accountid:60e96a31131bf80069e1459f] - Please see below the email we received today from DLA + their proposed speaking points for the meeting with ANA. Please let me know if you need anything further before your meeting with ANA next week (bearing in mind that I’m off next week 😉 ).

+DLA email:+

In the very unfortunate absence of response by the City Council, please find hereunder the speaking points summing up our research and legal analysis. Please also find them attached in briefing form.

We are willing to lay them in a (more formal) Legal Memo that you may share with ANA and this is something you may convey to them in the coming meeting, such as to strengthen your position. We will separately further complain to the City Council as regards their lack of response but for the moment we assume the meeting with ANA as the priority.

As you may see hereunder, we conclude that: 

*a)    ANA has a sufficient set of legal powers under the concession agreement to regulate (and therefore change) pick-up and drop-off points of transport service providers* (including taxis) in the Lisbon airport;

*b)*    Even if some occurrence took place leading ANA to waive its powers under the concession agreement and acknowledge the power of the City Council, *nothing prevents ANA from requesting to the City Council a change in the current disposal of pick-up and drop-off points*, if necessary supported by a submission by Bolt.

*c)    Presenting such a request to the City Council is not only an option at the disposal of ANA but is actually an obligation, since the Competition Authority found ANA to be a dominant undertaking in the Lisbon airport* under competition law rules and, as such, subject to the obligation of avoiding any discrimination between transport service providers.

 

+*SPEAKING POINTS*+

·         We have consulted with our legal advisers and our opinion is that the legal set of powers resulting from the concession agreement between the Portuguese State and ANA concerning the Portuguese airports provides ANA with sufficient powers to take decisions in respect of the location of taxi passenger pick-up points, which covers the Lisbon airport.

·         The source of these powers is Decree-Law No. 254/2012, of November 28, the statute that establishes the general regime for the provision of the public airport service in support of civil aviation in Portugal, which is exclusively granted to ANA. The concession agreement derives from and is based on this statute.

·         Article 7(1) (a) and (g) of Decree-Law No. 254/2012 provide that  “_the concessionaire has the powers and prerogatives of the grantor regarding: a) the licensing of the occupation and exercise of activities and services in assets of the public airport domain included within the scope of the concession, as well as regarding the practice of all acts relating to the execution, modification and cancellation of licenses and g) the preparation and application of regulatory standards within the scope of the concession activity, particularly in matters of security, environment and access and use of services included in the airport activities and services_".

·         “Airport Activities and Services”, as provided for in Clause 5 of the Concession Agreement and its Annexes, include the "_organization of airport spaces, as well as the discipline of their occupation and use_" (§17), the “_modal transfer between all means of transport available at the airports_" (§ 18), the "_provision of public car parking spaces_” (§ 19) and "_any other activities and services deemed necessary for the safe and efficient operation of airport infrastructures_" (§21).

·         In addition, the Concession Areas defined in Annex 2 to the concession agreement include the parking areas of Lisbon Airport as well as the areas designated for the "pick up" of passengers by vehicles.

·         We do not ignore the fact that general law (Decree-Law 251/98, of 11 August 1998) attributes to the municipalities (city councils) the power to regulate taxi parking. However, this applies to standard areas within cities and not to areas under an exceptional regime as is the case of concession areas such as the Lisbon airport. In our opinion, the exceptional powers granted to ANA by the concession agreement apply to the exceptional area comprising the Lisbon airport and therefore ANA holds the appropriate powers to determine pick-up and drop-off points in the airport area.

·         ANA shared this opinion until quite recently. In response to information requests by the Portuguese Competition Authority (“PCA”) in 2015 in the context of a project between ANTRAL, the Lisbon City Council and ANA aiming at establishing a single tariff for taxi transport services originating at the Lisbon airport, ANA stressed its role as the concessionaire and sole licensing entity for the occupation and exercise of activities and services in public domain areas located within the airport. Furthermore, ANA referred to a draft "Regulation on access to the airport terminals of the Lisbon, Porto and Faro airports by taxi mode", through which it intended "_not only to promote the control and discipline of the taxi operation areas, but also to establish higher standards of customer service quality, with all the resulting benefits for the end consumers of this type of transport service_".

·         In light of this stance that was publicly disclosed by the PCA, it is worth questioning whether and why ANA have changed their position.

·         Even if there has been an occurrence leading ANA to acknowledge the municipality’s power and to waive their own powers under the concession agreement, the matter of fact is that nothing prevents ANA from requesting to the City Council a change in the current disposal of pick-up and drop-off points. If ANA considers that it should not submit such request on its own motion and that it requires a particular reason to do so, Bolt is willing to formally submit such a request to ANA so that it may use such request to ground its submission to the City Council.

·         Bolt considers that submitting such a request to the City Council is not only an option available to ANA but is actually an obligation incumbent upon ANA.

·         In fact, in its Recommendation on the Introduction of a Single Tariff for the Provision of Taxi Services Originating in the Portela Airport of 21 January 2016, the PCA has found ANA to be a dominant undertaking in the provision of support services to civil aviation in the Lisbon airport and has stressed the special responsibility that ANA is accordingly subject to under competition law rules. Among the several duties resulting from this special responsibility, the PCA has underlined the duty of ANA to avoid any discrimination between transport service providers, “_namely as regards conditions concerning access to the concession area by transport service providers, to ensure that such conditions are not capable of creating competition distortions, particularly where uneven competition conditions between providers are created which are not appropriate and indispensable to the pursuit of the public interest in the context of the concession_”.

·         Bolt considers that the current disposal of the pick-up and drop-off points at the Lisbon airport unduly discriminates between transport service providers to the detriment of TVDE providers. The current disposal unduly favours taxi service providers and thereby creates a serious competition distortion that is not required by the pursuit of the public interest in the context of the concession. In addition, Bolt considers that such discrimination is not appropriate, nor necessary, since physical conditions at the airport allow for the accommodation of a solution that equalizes competition conditions between taxi and TVDE service providers.

·         Bolt considers that ANA is under a legal obligation to terminate the current discrimination by any means at its disposal and that failure to do so might entail ANA’s liability under competition law rules.

On partial refunds:

* The main input is it makes sense to take the refund from a single invoice.
* CS is marking who is in fault in case of a partial refund. So Commerce team can act based on this input when it comes to how to reflect the refund. If the Driver is in fault, it makes sense to take the refund amount from the ride fare invoice. If Bolt is in fault, we are refunding the money from our pocket anyway so we do not need to take the money from either invoices (in other words, we need to make sure the Driver gets the promised sum entirely).
* Considering partial refunds mostly happen out of good will - it is not a reversing of the service, but rather compensating after the service. So, different VAT rates don't make much difference here since we are not reversing the money but paying extra from our pocket.

{code:sql}  WITH failed as (
 SELECT bi.id,
        bi.country,
        bi.created AS company_created,
        bi.created AS payment_created,
        bi.balance / r.rate as amount_euro,
        'failed' AS payment_status
 FROM glue.ng_public.business_invoicing_business_company bi
 LEFT join glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON bi.currency = r.currency AND DATE (r.valid_on) = DATE (bi.created)
 WHERE
   bi.balance < 0
  AND bi.invoice_type = 'claim'
  AND bi.credit_limit = 0
  AND bi.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND bi.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
 ), other AS (
 SELECT
    co.id,
    co.country,
    co.created AS company_created,
    p.created AS payment_created,
    pr.amount / r.rate AS amount_euro,
    CASE WHEN (ppr.state <> 'ignored') OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') THEN 'fraud' else p.state end as payment_status
FROM
    glue.ng_public.business_business_company co
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment_user u ON u.external_id=co.id AND u.type='business'
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment_order po ON po.payment_user_id=u.id
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment as p ON p.payment_order_id = po.id
    JOIN
    glue.ng_public.payment_payment_row pr ON pr.id = p.last_payment_row_id
    LEFT JOIN
    glue.ng_public.fraud_user_latest_payment_problem as ppr ON ppr.payment_id = p.id
    LEFT JOIN
    glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON p.currency = r.currency AND DATE (r.valid_on) = DATE (p.created)
WHERE
  co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND p.state <> 'prepare'
  AND p.state <> 'created'
  AND u.type='business'
  AND po.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND po.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND p.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND p.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND pr.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND pr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND ppr.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
  AND ppr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
payments AS (
select *
FROM
    failed
UNION
SELECT *
from other
),
inputs AS (
SELECT 
d.id AS calculation_id,
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.device_additional_info.carrier_name') AS device_carrier,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.phone_check.carrier_name') AS phone_carrier
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request AS d
WHERE 
d.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
)
SELECT 
CAST(i.device_carrier AS varchar) || ':' || CAST(i.phone_carrier AS varchar) || ':' || cast(o.country as varchar) as key,
		COUNT (DISTINCT o.user_id) AS count_of_users,
		COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS count_of_companies,
		COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_companies_with_failed_payments,
		COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_companies_with_fraud_payments,
		(COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN  p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS failed_company_ratio,
		(COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' then p.id else null end) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) AS fraud_company_ratio
FROM
    glue.ng_public.company_order o
join 
payments p ON p.id = cast(split_part(o.payment_method_id,'-',1) as bigint)
JOIN inputs AS i ON i.order_id = o.search_token AND i.user_id = o.user_id 
where
	o.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
	AND o.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
	AND o.state = 'finished'
    AND o.payment_method_type = 'business'
GROUP BY 1
HAVING COUNT (DISTINCT p.id) > 5
   AND (
   (( COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='failed' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id)) > 0.3
or
 (( COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.payment_status='fraud' THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) * 1.00)/ COUNT (DISTINCT p.id)) >  0.3
 ){code}

_Fraud Team Blocks vs CS/OPS Fraud Blocks 

Some might argue that CS and local ops are helping out the Fraud team by blocking fraudulent users and users linked to fraudsters and thus reducing fraud costs. This might be true in some cases but overall, it is much better for Bolt if fraud blocking is done only by the Fraud team:

Fewer false-positives. Fraud has much better visibility into the users' data and can better spot good users. Also, when CS/OPS hard-blocks a user it is very hard for them to recover their account. Fraud team uses a much more fine-tuned approach- depending on the type of risk we will require you to authenticate the payment with 3DS or ask you to verify your documents with Veriff. This leads to much less friction for the customer.  

Consistent logic based on data. Fraud team's decisions are based on the analysis of fraud patterns taking into account potential fraud savings and false positives. All the fraud decisions are logged and we use that data to later analyze and improve the rules. CS/OPS decisions are based on the gut feel of an agent who doesn't have extensive fraud experience. 

Detection of patterns and bigger impact. CS handles one case at a time which is not scalable. Fraud team analyzes fraud patterns and creates rules that prevent the same type of fraud from happening in multiple markets. 

It is clearly better if fraud-related blocks are done only by the Fraud team. The CS and local ops can help out by escalating cases to the Fraud team when they spot bigger trends._

{code:sql}SELECT x.key,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_failed_payments,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS failed_payment_count_ratio,
SUM(x.price_eur) AS amount_of_in_app_orders,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_fraud_payments,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_failed_payments,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS fraud_payment_amount_ratio,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS failed_payment_amount_ratio
FROM (
SELECT cast(REGEXP_REPLACE(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.device_additional_info.device_fingerprint'), '[\\r\\n|]+', '-')as varchar) || ':' || cast(co.city_id as varchar) AS key,
co.user_id AS user_id,
co.order_id AS order_id,
co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem OR co.is_chargeback THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payment,
CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS failed_payment
FROM glue.ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN glue.archive_analytical.user_rental_request d ON co.fraud_calculation_id = d.id  
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND co.order_type = 'rental'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) AS x
WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING 
	COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) > 1
	AND (
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 1
	OR COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 0
	)
	AND (
	((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0)) > 0.2
	OR ((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0)) > 0.2
	)
ORDER BY
	fraud_payment_count_ratio DESC,
	failed_payment_count_ratio desc{code}

Having now done some work in the react-commons monorepo now, my thoughts on this (way to long, will tl;dr summarise when I have time):

Summary:

{{deps-check}} looks like it’s made to solve our problem, but it’s extra tooling and we might be able to solve things with just peerDependencies (uh…).

We should check/improve pnpm config (and utilise all it’s options), properly declare dependencies between local packages and what is peer/dev/normal.

We should be vigilant in having everything in the repo work “as cloned” without any fixes we may have applied locally.



* Before introducing tooling, we can improve things just with cleanup/clarity
** carefully configure {{pnpm}} at the workspace root (who has {{shamefully-hoist}}, who has {{strict-peer-dependencies}} etc) and try to avoid configurations in packages, also what {{pnpm}} version are we all using (the {{engines}} field) does seem important so we get the exact same `node_modules` layout
** clean up what is a peerDependency and a dependency (and also a devDependency but I guess it doesn’t actually matter) in packages like {{react-uikit}} , because right now it’s all mixed up
** have a clear strategy for using {{peerDependencies}} and maybe configure {{pnpm}} to actually install them by default
*** [alternatives section in rnx-kit docs]([https://microsoft.github.io/rnx-kit/docs/architecture/dependency-management#alternatives|https://microsoft.github.io/rnx-kit/docs/architecture/dependency-management#alternatives|smart-link]) actually mentions that just {{peerDependencies}} and carefully setting version ranges is an alternative to using {{deps-check}} , but maybe the problems they mention (monorepo uses pnpm, our app uses yarn, other apps ? / “carefully setting version ranges” lol) are exactly the problems for us so we should just go straight for {{deps-check}} and completely ignore peer dependencies.
* on the react native version upgrade pain
** this seems to be exactly what {{rnx-kit}} {{deps-check}} solves, if various packages and apps really need to depend on different versions
*** as long as it is well maintained (everyone always promises…) because right now it looks like it doesn’t have all that many profiles? Solving this with “just” consistent use of package manager features (align everyone on pnpm, use peerDependencies + {{auto-install-peers}}, {{strict-peer-dependencies}} ) is very appealing to me for just having less tooling, but maybe infeasible.
*** it’s interesting that the {{deps-check}} idea is to have a blessed constellation of third party packages, kind of like the idea I had of just always using the expo blessed constellation and upgrading it with expo SDK releases (without necessarily using expo)
** in the (much much much less shared/important) monorepo for my previous app, what I did was always depend on these problematic dependencies with {{*}} in packages and then upgrade them across the entire monorepo via resolutions. Convenient, but might not scale for us (because packages really do need different versions, because our apps aren’t inside the monorepo)
* I think metro symlink issues should be solvable
** and our metro config might just shrink away at some point
** we can resolve symlinks now, with {{@rnx-kit/metro-resolver-symlinks}} (but I guess that’s buggy?, there’s a similar tool from expo that I used previously) and I read in the “what improvements should react native get” thread that it does actually support symlinks already, but something is missing for full {{pnpm}} / workspaces support (maybe it was watching?)
** instead of manually configuring extra local packages in metro, we can try to add them to {{package.json}} dependencies and rely on {{pnpm}} to symlink them, maybe do so with the {{workspace:}} protocol because it provides some more safety and warnings on versions. Might still need the manual watch config.

this inject option [https://pnpm.io/package_json#dependenciesmetainjected|https://pnpm.io/package_json#dependenciesmetainjected|smart-link] seems relevant, maybe, but I’m not sure what it solves for us

{code:sql}SELECT x.key,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_failed_payments,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS failed_payment_count_ratio,
SUM(x.price_eur) AS amount_of_in_app_orders,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_fraud_payments,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_failed_payments,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS fraud_payment_amount_ratio,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS failed_payment_amount_ratio
FROM (
SELECT json_extract_scalar(r.input, '$.data.device_uid') || ':' || cast(co.city_id as varchar) AS key,
co.user_id AS user_id,
co.order_id AS order_id,
co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem OR co.is_chargeback THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payment,
CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS failed_payment
FROM glue.ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN glue.archive_analytical.user_rental_request r ON co.fraud_calculation_id = r.id  
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND r.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND co.order_type = 'rental'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) AS x
WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING 
	COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) > 1
	AND (
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 1
	OR COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 0
	)
	AND (
	((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0)) > 0.2
	OR ((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0)) > 0.2
	)
ORDER BY
	fraud_payment_count_ratio DESC,
	failed_payment_count_ratio desc{code}

* *Conclusions:*
** ASP does not depend on spending, so it doesn’t seem feasible to forecast ASP at different levels of ASP.
** Still, we can provide ASP forecasts at city and daily level with a MAPE of, at least, 7.5%. We could reduce this number with hyperparameter tuning and higher model complexity.

{code:sql}SELECT x.key,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_failed_payments,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS failed_payment_count_ratio,
SUM(x.price_eur) AS amount_of_in_app_orders,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_fraud_payments,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_failed_payments,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS fraud_payment_amount_ratio,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS failed_payment_amount_ratio
FROM (
SELECT json_extract_scalar(r.input, '$.additional.car.card_bin') || ':' || cast(co.city_id as varchar) AS key,
co.user_id AS user_id,
co.order_id AS order_id,
co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem OR co.is_chargeback THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payment,
CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS failed_payment
FROM glue.ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN glue.archive_analytical.user_rental_request r ON co.fraud_calculation_id = r.id  
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND r.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND co.order_type = 'rental'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
and co.payment_method_type <> 'applepay'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) AS x
WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING 
	COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) > 1
	AND (
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 1
	OR COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 0
	)
	AND (
	((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0)) > 0.2
	OR ((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0)) > 0.2
	)
ORDER BY
	fraud_payment_count_ratio DESC,
	failed_payment_count_ratio desc{code}

* 3.14 eur is Bolt fee/commission → this is what Bolt gets & is paid by the provider
* 1.74 eur is the delivery fee → in this case the ROD provider gets this one (usually it’s the courier) & is paid by the eater
* 1.5 eur is the delivery campaign → this is what the eater gets & is paid by Bolt

Now quickly summarising the above:

* Provider receives 20.9 - 3.14 + 1.74
* Eater pays 20.9 + 1.74 - 1.5

{code:sql}SELECT x.key,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_failed_payments,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0) AS failed_payment_count_ratio,
SUM(x.price_eur) AS amount_of_in_app_orders,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_fraud_payments,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_of_failed_payments,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS fraud_payment_amount_ratio,
(SUM(CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.price_eur ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / NULLIF(SUM(x.price_eur),0) AS failed_payment_amount_ratio
FROM (
SELECT 	CASE WHEN json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.device_additional_info.carrier_name') = ' ' OR json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.device_additional_info.carrier_name') IS NULL THEN 'EMPTY' ELSE REGEXP_REPLACE(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.device_additional_info.carrier_name'), '[\\r\\n|]+', '-') END 
		|| '::' ||
		CASE WHEN json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.phone_check.carrier_name') = ' ' OR json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.phone_check.carrier_name') IS NULL THEN 'EMPTY_phone' ELSE REGEXP_REPLACE(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.phone_check.carrier_name'), '[\\r\\n|]+', '-') END 
		|| ':' ||  cast(co.city_id as varchar) AS KEY,
co.user_id AS user_id,
co.order_id AS order_id,
co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem OR co.is_chargeback THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payment,
CASE WHEN co.is_final_failed_payment THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS failed_payment
FROM glue.ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
LEFT JOIN glue.archive_analytical.user_rental_request d ON co.fraud_calculation_id = d.id  
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
AND co.order_type = 'rental'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) AS x
WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
HAVING 
	COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) > 1
	AND (
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 1
	OR COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) > 0
	)
	AND (
	((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.failed_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0)) > 0.2
	OR ((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.fraud_payment IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id ELSE NULL END) * 1.0000000) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id),0)) > 0.2
	)
ORDER BY
	fraud_payment_count_ratio DESC,
	failed_payment_count_ratio desc{code}
